<file path="src/products/design/modules/core/node/node-layout.types.ts">
import type { BoxSides } from "@canvas";
⋮----
/** Which way an auto layout lines its layers up. */
export type LayoutDirection = "horizontal" | "vertical";
⋮----
/**
 * Where an auto layout puts its layers along its direction: packed at the start, the middle or
 * the end, or spread so the first and last touch the padding (Figma's "Auto" gap).
 */
export type LayoutAlign = "start" | "center" | "end" | "space-between";
⋮----
/** Where an auto layout puts each layer across its direction (`baseline`: texts' first lines). */
export type LayoutCounterAlign = "start" | "center" | "end" | "baseline";
⋮----
/**
 * A frame's auto layout (Figma's): its layers placed one after another in `index` order, with
 * `gap` between them and `padding` round them; a frame whose size hugs them grows with them.
 */
export interface AutoLayout {
  direction: LayoutDirection;
  /** Whether layers that don't fit go on to new lines (rows or columns). */
  wrap: boolean;
  /** The space between layers along the direction (with `space-between`, used when it hugs). */
  gap: number;
  /** The space between wrapped lines. */
  counterGap: number;
  padding: BoxSides;
  align: LayoutAlign;
  counterAlign: LayoutCounterAlign;
  /** Whether layers' strokes outside their box take space, as Figma's "Strokes included". */
  strokesIncluded: boolean;
  /** Whether the first layer is drawn on top (Figma's "Canvas stacking: first on top"). */
  reverseStacking: boolean;
}
⋮----
/** Whether layers that don't fit go on to new lines (rows or columns). */
⋮----
/** The space between layers along the direction (with `space-between`, used when it hugs). */
⋮----
/** The space between wrapped lines. */
⋮----
/** Whether layers' strokes outside their box take space, as Figma's "Strokes included". */
⋮----
/** Whether the first layer is drawn on top (Figma's "Canvas stacking: first on top"). */
⋮----
/**
 * How a layer's width or height is decided: kept (`fixed`), the size of what it holds (`hug`, an
 * auto layout frame or a text) or the room its auto layout parent leaves (`fill`).
 */
export type LayoutSizing = "fixed" | "hug" | "fill";
⋮----
/** A layer's sizing on each axis: `h` its width, `v` its height. */
export interface NodeSizing {
  h: LayoutSizing;
  v: LayoutSizing;
}
⋮----
/** The smallest and largest a layer may become in an auto layout (unset: no limit). */
export interface SizeLimits {
  minW?: number;
  maxW?: number;
  minH?: number;
  maxH?: number;
}
⋮----
/** One axis of a box: `h` (x and width) or `v` (y and height). */
export type LayoutAxis = keyof NodeSizing;
</file>

<file path=".github/workflows/release.yml">
# Builds a release when a version tag is pushed (`pnpm release:tag 0.2.0` pushes `v0.2.0`).
#
# Everything lands in a DRAFT release: the Windows installer, the Ubuntu .deb, the AppImage, the
# Arch package, the updater signatures and `latest.json`. Installed apps only see the update once
# the draft is published on GitHub.
#
# Needs the repository secrets TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY and TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD
# (from `pnpm tauri signer generate`), which sign the files the updater downloads.
name: Release

on:
push:
tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
contents: write

concurrency:
group: release-${{ github.ref_name }}
cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
create-release:
name: Create the draft release
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
outputs:
release-id: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.id }}
steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check the tag matches the app's version
        run: |
          version=$(jq -r .version src-tauri/tauri.conf.json)
          if [ "v$version" != "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" ]; then
            echo "::error::Tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME doesn't match tauri.conf.json's version $version"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Create the draft
        id: draft
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --draft --generate-notes \
            --title "Cloudy Canvas $GITHUB_REF_NAME" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          id=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases" \
            --jq "map(select(.tag_name == \"$GITHUB_REF_NAME\" and .draft)) | first | .id")
          echo "id=$id" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

build:
name: Build (${{ matrix.name }})
needs: create-release
strategy:
fail-fast: false
matrix:
include: - name: Windows
os: windows-latest
bundles: nsis # The oldest supported Ubuntu, so the AppImage runs on more distros. - name: Linux
os: ubuntu-22.04
bundles: deb,appimage
runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Linux dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libappindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev build-essential patchelf

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 12

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: lts/*
          cache: pnpm

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: src-tauri -> target

      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          NO_STRIP: "true"
        with:
          releaseId: ${{ needs.create-release.outputs.release-id }}
          includeUpdaterJson: true
          updaterJsonPreferNsis: true
          args: --config src-tauri/tauri.release.conf.json --bundles ${{ matrix.bundles }}

arch:
name: Build (Arch Linux)
needs: [create-release, build]
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
container: archlinux:latest
steps: - name: Install build tools
run: |
pacman -Syu --noconfirm --needed base-devel git github-cli nodejs pnpm rustup \
webkit2gtk-4.1 gtk3 libsoup3 librsvg openssl

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # makepkg refuses to run as root.
      - name: Build the package
        run: |
          useradd -m builder
          chown -R builder "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          runuser -u builder -- env HOME=/home/builder bash -euc '
            cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
            rustup default stable
            pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
            pnpm release:arch
          '

      - name: Upload it to the draft
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          git config --global --add safe.directory "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          gh release upload "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" packaging/arch/*.pkg.tar.zst --clobber \
            --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"

</file>

<file path="src/canvas/render/effects/effect-renderer.types.ts">
import type { Texture } from "pixi.js";
⋮----
import type { CanvasEffect } from "../../effects";
import type { Rect } from "../../geometry.types";
import type { EffectShader } from "./effect-shader";
⋮----
/**
 * When an effect is drawn in the pipeline, in this order: what shows through from behind
 * (`backdrop`: background blur, glass), what's laid on the content (`content`: inner shadows,
 * noise, texture), what's cast behind it (`behind`: drop shadows) and what changes the whole
 * result (`filter`: layer blur, shaders). Effects of one stage go in list order.
 */
export type EffectStage = "backdrop" | "content" | "behind" | "filter";
⋮----
/**
 * What a renderer draws with while a scope's effects are applied, on the GPU. Lengths are CSS
 * pixels of the filter's textures (`px` turns world units into them); textures from `texture()`,
 * `run` and `blur` go back to the pool when the scope is done.
 */
export interface EffectPass {
  /** The scope's content as drawn, before any effect. */
  readonly content: Texture;
  /**
   * What's behind the scope on the canvas, for renderers that read it (`backdrop`); a blank
   * texture otherwise.
   */
  readonly backdrop: Texture;
  /** CSS pixels per world unit (the zoom on screen, 1 in exports). */
  readonly scale: number;
  /** World lengths in CSS pixels. */
  px(world: number): number;
  /** A world offset (dx, dy) in the element's turned frame, in CSS pixels on screen. */
  offset(dx: number, dy: number): { x: number; y: number };
  /** The element's own box (unturned, world units). */
  readonly box: Rect;
  /**
   * The affine map (a, b, c, d, tx, ty: `x = a·u + c·v + tx`, `y = b·u + d·v + ty`) from texture
   * coordinates to the element's own coordinates (unturned, from its top-left corner), so a
   * shader can lay things on the element (progressive blur, noise that stays put, light).
   */
  readonly toLocal: readonly [number, number, number, number, number, number];
  /** A blank texture the size of the content. */
  texture(): Texture;
  /** Draws `shader` over `input` (its `uTexture`) into a new texture, or into `output`. */
  run(shader: EffectShader, input: Texture, output?: Texture): Texture;
  /** A Gaussian blur of `input` (`radius` is Figma's: twice the deviation, in CSS pixels). */
  blur(input: Texture, radius: number): Texture;
}
⋮----
/** The scope's content as drawn, before any effect. */
⋮----
/**
   * What's behind the scope on the canvas, for renderers that read it (`backdrop`); a blank
   * texture otherwise.
   */

/** CSS pixels per world unit (the zoom on screen, 1 in exports). */
⋮----
/** World lengths in CSS pixels. */

/** A world offset (dx, dy) in the element's turned frame, in CSS pixels on screen. */

/** The element's own box (unturned, world units). */
⋮----
/**
   * The affine map (a, b, c, d, tx, ty: `x = a·u + c·v + tx`, `y = b·u + d·v + ty`) from texture
   * coordinates to the element's own coordinates (unturned, from its top-left corner), so a
   * shader can lay things on the element (progressive blur, noise that stays put, light).
   */
⋮----
/** A blank texture the size of the content. */
texture(): Texture;
/** Draws `shader` over `input` (its `uTexture`) into a new texture, or into `output`. */
run(shader: EffectShader, input: Texture, output?: Texture): Texture;
/** A Gaussian blur of `input` (`radius` is Figma's: twice the deviation, in CSS pixels). */
blur(input: Texture, radius: number): Texture;
⋮----
/**
 * How one type of effect is drawn: an engine-side piece a product contributes (the design's
 * shadows, blurs, noise, glass, shaders). It works on the GPU through `EffectPass`.
 */
export interface EffectRenderer<E extends CanvasEffect = CanvasEffect> {
  type: string;
  stage: EffectStage;
  /** Whether its effects may read what's behind the scope (the canvas then keeps a back buffer). */
  readonly backdrop?: boolean;
  /** Whether this effect does (a shader whose code reads it); `backdrop` when left out. */
  readsBackdrop?(effect: E): boolean;
  /**
   * How far past the content the result can show, in world units, given how far it did before
   * (`outset`): a shadow's reach is the most of either, a blur adds its own.
   */
  outset(effect: E, outset: number): number;
  /**
   * How far past the content it needs to read, in world units (a backdrop blur samples beyond
   * the shape); `outset` when left out.
   */
  margin?(effect: E): number;
  /** Draws the effect over `current` (the pipeline so far) and returns the new result. */
  render(pass: EffectPass, effect: E, current: Texture): Texture;
}
⋮----
/** Whether its effects may read what's behind the scope (the canvas then keeps a back buffer). */
⋮----
/** Whether this effect does (a shader whose code reads it); `backdrop` when left out. */
readsBackdrop?(effect: E): boolean;
/**
   * How far past the content the result can show, in world units, given how far it did before
   * (`outset`): a shadow's reach is the most of either, a blur adds its own.
   */
outset(effect: E, outset: number): number;
/**
   * How far past the content it needs to read, in world units (a backdrop blur samples beyond
   * the shape); `outset` when left out.
   */
margin?(effect: E): number;
/** Draws the effect over `current` (the pipeline so far) and returns the new result. */
render(pass: EffectPass, effect: E, current: Texture): Texture;
⋮----
/** A product's effect renderers by type. */
export type EffectRenderers = ReadonlyMap<string, EffectRenderer>;

 * the deviation `uSigma` in taps. Outside the frame counts as transparent.

 * A shadow's shape: the input's opacity moved by `uOffset` (CSS pixels), grown (`uSpread` > 0)

⋮----

⋮----

⋮----
/**
 * Lays `uLayer` over the input inside `uContent`'s shape (premultiplied "atop"): an inner
 * shadow, noise. `uShape` > 0 makes the shape opaque wherever the content shows at all, so
 * translucent fills take it fully.
 */
⋮----
/* glsl */ `${FILTER_HEADER}
⋮----
/**
 * Lays `uLayer` under the input inside `uContent`'s shape (opaque wherever the content shows at
 * all, so a translucent fill shows it fully): what's behind, blurred or refracted.

  pk: boolean;
  increment: boolean;
  notNull: boolean;
  unique: boolean;
  /** Raw DBML default value (e.g. `0`, `'draft'`, `` `now()` ``), or `null` for none. */
  default: string | null;

}

⋮----
/** A freehand stroke. */

  type: "stroke";
  pen: StrokePen;
  color: string;
  /** Thickness in world units. */
  size: number;
  /** Flat [x0, y0, x1, y1, …] list, relative to (x, y). */
  points: number[];
}
⋮----
/** Thickness in world units. */
⋮----
/** Flat [x0, y0, x1, y1, …] list, relative to (x, y). */
⋮----
/** How each pen's outline is traced by perfect-freehand. */
export interface StrokePenLook {
  thinning: number;
  smoothing: number;
  streamline: number;
  /** Rounded ends (flat when false). */
  caps: boolean;
  /** Fill opacity. */
  alpha: number;
}
⋮----
/** Rounded ends (flat when false). */
⋮----
/** Fill opacity. */
⋮----

  pen: StrokePen;

  smoothTolerance: number;

  smoothPasses: number;
  /** The largest thickness agents may set, in world units. */

}

}

import type { ChildResolveContext } from "./child-host.types";
import { DesignNodeKind } from "./design-node.kind";
import type { DesignNode } from "./design-node.types";
⋮----
/**
 * The base of nodes made of their children (groups, booleans): a click on a child selects them
 * (until they're entered), turning, scaling and flipping them does it to their children, and
 * their geometry follows the children (`resolveFromChildren`, run by the core's `resolveTree`).
 * They aren't containers: nothing is dropped into them on the canvas.
 */
export abstract class ChildHostKind<E extends DesignNode = DesignNode> extends DesignNodeKind<E>
⋮----
/**
   * The node as its children make it (bounds, and whatever else it derives), from the children
   * already resolved. The result is the scene's, never stored.
   */
abstract resolveFromChildren(
    el: E,
    children: readonly CanvasElement[],
    context: ChildResolveContext,
  ): E;
⋮----
/** Nothing of its own is hit by default: a click reaches its children. */
override hitTest(_el: E, _p: Point, _tolerance: number): boolean
⋮----
/** Turning it turns its children (its members); it stays the box round them. */
override rotate(): ElementPatch<E>
⋮----
/** Its turn is its children's: agents turn it with `rotate_nodes`. */
override completePatch(
    el: E,
    patch: ElementPatch<E>,
    context: ElementBuildContext,
): ElementPatch<E>
⋮----
/** Scaling it scales its children (its members). */
override scale(): ElementPatch<E>
⋮----
/** Flipping it flips its children (its members). */
override flip(): ElementPatch<E>
⋮----
/** Its outline is its children's, which a moved child would drag along: they're the targets. */
override snapTarget(): boolean
</file>

/** What every built-in effect has: its id, type and whether it shows. */
interface EffectBase<T extends string> extends NodeEffect {
  type: T;
}
⋮----
/** A colored effect's color: a hex color and its opacity (0–1). */
interface Colored {
  color: string;
  opacity: number;
}
⋮----
/** A shadow's placement: its offset, blur and spread, in world units. */
interface ShadowShape extends Colored {
  x: number;
  y: number;
  /** Figma's blur radius (twice the Gaussian's deviation). */
  blur: number;
  /** How much the shadow grows (or, negative, shrinks) before it's blurred. */
  spread: number;
}
⋮----
/** Figma's blur radius (twice the Gaussian's deviation). */
⋮----
/** How much the shadow grows (or, negative, shrinks) before it's blurred. */
⋮----
/** A shadow cast behind the layer. */
export interface DropShadowEffect extends EffectBase<"drop-shadow">, ShadowShape {
  /** Shows the shadow through the layer's translucent parts too (Figma's "Show behind"). */
  showBehind: boolean;
}
⋮----
/** Shows the shadow through the layer's translucent parts too (Figma's "Show behind"). */
⋮----
/** A shadow cast inside the layer from its edges. */
export interface InnerShadowEffect extends EffectBase<"inner-shadow">, ShadowShape {}
⋮----
/** The layer and what it holds blurred: evenly, or from `start` to `end` (progressive). */
export interface LayerBlurEffect extends EffectBase<"layer-blur"> {
  radius: number;
  progressive: boolean;
  /** Where a progressive blur starts and ends, in the layer's box (0–1 on each axis). */
  start: Point;
  end: Point;
  /** The blur at `start` (it grows to `radius` at `end`). */
  startRadius: number;
}
⋮----
/** Where a progressive blur starts and ends, in the layer's box (0–1 on each axis). */
⋮----
/** The blur at `start` (it grows to `radius` at `end`). */
⋮----
/** What's behind the layer blurred, showing through its translucent fills (frosted glass). */
export interface BackgroundBlurEffect extends EffectBase<"background-blur"> {
  radius: number;
}
⋮----
/** Grain over the layer: one color, two, or many. */
export interface NoiseEffect extends EffectBase<"noise">, Colored {
  noiseType: "mono" | "duo" | "multi";
  /** Grain size, world units. */
  size: number;
  /** How much of the layer the grain covers (0–1). */
  density: number;
  /** The second color of `duo` grain. */
  secondColor: string;
}
⋮----
/** Grain size, world units. */
⋮----
/** How much of the layer the grain covers (0–1). */
⋮----
/** The second color of `duo` grain. */
⋮----
/** The layer's edges and fills roughened, like paper or stone. */
export interface TextureEffect extends EffectBase<"texture"> {
  /** Grain size, world units. */
  size: number;
  /** How far edges are pushed, world units. */
  radius: number;
  /** Keeps the roughness inside the layer's shape. */
  clipToShape: boolean;
}
⋮----
/** Grain size, world units. */
⋮----
/** How far edges are pushed, world units. */
⋮----
/** Keeps the roughness inside the layer's shape. */
⋮----
/** Liquid glass: what's behind refracted at the edges, frosted, lit along its rim. */
export interface GlassEffect extends EffectBase<"glass"> {
  /** Degrees the light comes from (0 is the right, counterclockwise). */
  lightAngle: number;
  /** 0–1. */
  lightIntensity: number;
  /** How much the edges bend what's behind (0–1). */
  refraction: number;
  /** How far in from the edges the glass curves, world units. */
  depth: number;
  /** Rainbow fringes at the edges (0–1). */
  dispersion: number;
  /** Blur of what's behind, world units. */
  frost: number;
  /** How wide the light's highlight spreads round the rim (0–1). */
  splay: number;
}

export type VectorPart =
  | { kind: "handle"; segment: number; vertex: number }
  | { kind: "vertex"; vertex: number }

  | {
      kind: "points";
      start: CanvasPointer;
      origin: VectorElement;
      vertices: Set<number>;
      started: boolean;
    }
  | {
      kind: "handle";
      origin: VectorElement;
      segment: number;
      vertex: number;
      mirror: boolean;
      started: boolean;
    }
  | { kind: "marquee"; start: CanvasPointer; origin: VectorElement; base: Set<number> };
⋮----

}

/** A point of a glyph's outline, in pixels (y grows down). */

/** One closed outline of a glyph (the canvas's `PathContour` has the same shape). */

  start: GlyphPoint;

}
⋮----
/** A shaped glyph: its outlines placed at the pen (on the baseline), and how far it moves it. */

  advance: number;

/** One line of text shaped in a face at a size, with the face's ascent and descent there. */

}
⋮----
/**
 * Turns text into glyph outlines (kerning, ligatures and complex scripts shaped as the font says),
 * so text can be flattened or combined. A face is read the first time it's asked for: until then
 * `shape` answers `null`, and `onReady` reports when it can.
 */

  shape(font: FontRequest, text: string, size: number): ShapedLine | null;
  /** Calls `listener` with each face once it's ready. Returns the unsubscribe. */
  onReady(listener: (font: FontRequest) => void): () => void;
}

/**
 * Where checking and installing stand: `available` until the user acts on it, `downloading` with
 * the share done (`null` while the size is unknown), then `restarting`.
 */
export type UpdateStatus =
  | { phase: "idle" }
  | { phase: "checking" }
  | { phase: "upToDate" }
  | { phase: "error"; message: string }
  | { phase: "available"; update: AvailableUpdate }
  | { phase: "downloading"; update: AvailableUpdate; progress: number | null }
  | { phase: "restarting"; update: AvailableUpdate };
⋮----
export interface CheckOptions {
  /** A background check: errors are only logged, not shown. */
  silent?: boolean;
}

  installKind: InstallKind | null;
  /** The version whose notice was closed with "Later", hidden until the next start. */
  dismissed: string | null;
  check: (options?: CheckOptions) => Promise<void>;
  /** Installs the available update, or opens its download page for a package install. */
  install: () => Promise<void>;
  dismiss: () => void;
}

<file path="src-tauri/icons/source/app-icon.svg">
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1024" height="1024" viewBox="0 0 1024 1024">
  <!-- Cloudy Canvas app icon: the "foca watona" (spotted seal) peeking over a canvas.
       Colors from src/shared/ui/styles/tokens.css (oklch converted to sRGB hex):
       ice-500 #4799d9, ice-600 #2479bc, seal-50 #f9fafc, seal-100 #f0f3f6, seal-300 #cfd5db,
       seal-400 #a4acb4, seal-900 #202730, blush-300 #ffbaa8. -->
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="fur" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#cfd5db"/>
      <stop offset="0.75" stop-color="#f0f3f6"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>

  <!-- Tile: sharp square, 56px radius (5.5%), 48px padding -->
  <rect x="48" y="48" width="928" height="928" rx="56" fill="#4799d9"/>

  <!-- Artwork drawn in the logo's 64-unit space, scaled 13.5x -->
  <g transform="translate(80 54) scale(13.5)" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">
    <!-- Body -->
    <ellipse cx="32" cy="28" rx="20" ry="16.5" fill="url(#fur)" stroke="#202730" stroke-width="2.6"/>
    <!-- Spots: few and large -->
    <ellipse cx="24" cy="16" rx="2.2" ry="1.5" fill="#a4acb4"/>
    <ellipse cx="38.5" cy="14.5" rx="2.4" ry="1.6" fill="#a4acb4"/>
    <ellipse cx="45" cy="20" rx="1.7" ry="1.3" fill="#a4acb4"/>
    <!-- Blush cheeks -->
    <ellipse cx="19" cy="26.3" rx="3.4" ry="2.1" fill="#ffbaa8"/>
    <ellipse cx="45" cy="26.3" rx="3.4" ry="2.1" fill="#ffbaa8"/>
    <!-- Closed eyes -->
    <path d="M20.8 23q3.4-3.6 6.8 0M36.4 23q3.4-3.6 6.8 0" fill="none" stroke="#202730" stroke-width="2.6"/>
    <!-- Muzzle and nose -->
    <path d="M32 26.2c-1-1.6-5.6-1.6-6 1.4-.3 2.4 2.6 3.4 4.4 2.6.8-.3 1.3-.8 1.6-1.3.3.5.8 1 1.6 1.3 1.8.8 4.7-.2 4.4-2.6-.4-3-5-3-6-1.4z" fill="#f9fafc" stroke="#202730" stroke-width="2"/>
    <ellipse cx="32" cy="25.9" rx="2" ry="1.35" fill="#202730"/>
    <!-- Canvas -->
    <rect x="8" y="33" width="48" height="25" rx="1.2" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#202730" stroke-width="2.6"/>
    <path d="M15 51c4-6 8-6 11-2s7 4 11-1" fill="none" stroke="#2479bc" stroke-width="2.8"/>
    <circle cx="45.5" cy="45" r="3.4" fill="#ffbaa8"/>
    <!-- Flippers on the canvas edge -->
    <ellipse cx="17.5" cy="34.5" rx="4.8" ry="2.8" transform="rotate(-18 17.5 34.5)" fill="#cfd5db" stroke="#202730" stroke-width="2.6"/>
    <ellipse cx="46.5" cy="34.5" rx="4.8" ry="2.8" transform="rotate(18 46.5 34.5)" fill="#cfd5db" stroke="#202730" stroke-width="2.6"/>
  </g>
</svg>

<file path="docs/er-language.md">
# ER diagrams: language and visual editor

Cloudy Canvas draws **Entity–Relationship diagrams** in Chen notation, including the extended model: hierarchies, aggregation and constraints. You can build them two ways, and both edit the same diagram:

- With the **visual editor**. Select a shape and use the form in the **ER diagram** panel, or use the **Add** menu.
- With **text**, in the panel's **Text** tab, using the language described below.

The shapes are the source of truth, and the text is a view of them. Everything is matched **by name** (then by position, for renames), so renaming something in the text keeps its place on the board. New shapes are laid out automatically. You can drag anything you like, and **Re-layout** tidies the whole diagram again.

A board can hold **several ER diagrams**. Each one has its own text, layout and names, so two diagrams side by side can both have a `Cliente` entity. Selecting any shape shows its diagram in the panel.

The rule ids (**S1**…) match the syntax review, so you can refer to them ("S18: rename `Isa` to …").

---

## Getting started

1. Press **E** (or use the ER button in the toolbar) and click the board. A new diagram starts with one entity, and the panel opens.
2. Either fill in the form, or open **Text** and paste a whole model. Pasting over the first entity lays the diagram out fresh where that entity was.
3. **Double-click** any entity, relation, attribute or aggregation on the board to rename it in place.

The panel header has six controls:

| Control                 | What it does                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Diagram name and ⌄**  | Renames the shown diagram, lists the board's diagrams (picking one takes you to it) and starts a **New diagram**.                                          |
| **+ Add**               | Adds an entity, relation, hierarchy, aggregation or constraint. It starts from the selection when that makes sense (for example, "Relation from Cliente"). |
| **Egg / circle button** | Switches attributes between Chen ellipses and lollipop circles (S21).                                                                                      |
| **Select button**       | Selects the whole shown diagram, so you can drag it as one.                                                                                                |
| **Grid button**         | Re-layout of the shown diagram. One undo reverts it.                                                                                                       |
| **×**                   | Closes the panel.                                                                                                                                          |

---

## Part A: Basics

**S1. Comments:** `// one line` or `/* several lines */`.

**S2. Names:** letters (accents included), digits and `_`, for example `dirección`, `fecha_nac` or `Cliente2`.

- Quote anything else: `"fecha de nacimiento"`.
- Keywords are case-insensitive.

**S3. Settings** go in square brackets after a name, separated by commas: `[pk, multi]`.

**S4. One item per line** inside `{ … }`. A trailing comma is allowed.

---

## Part B: Entities and attributes

**S5. Entity.** The block is optional, so `Entity Producto` alone works.

```
Entity Cliente {
  dni [pk]
  nombre
}
```

**S6. Weak entity** (drawn as a double rectangle):

```
Entity Ejemplar [weak] {
  número [partial]
}
```

**S7. Attribute settings:**

| Setting                           | Short form (S10) | Meaning                      | Drawn as                                       |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `[pk]` (alias `[key]`)            | `*dni`           | Key attribute                | Underlined name (filled dot in lollipop style) |
| `[partial]`                       | `~número`        | Partial key of a weak entity | Dashed underline                               |
| `[multi]` (alias `[multivalued]`) | `+teléfono`      | Multivalued                  | Double ellipse                                 |
| `[derived]`                       | `/edad`          | Derived (calculated)         | Dashed ellipse                                 |
| `[optional]` (S8)                 | none             | Optional                     | Half-filled circle in lollipop style           |

**S9. Composite attribute.** Its parts fan out from it:

```
  dirección {
    calle
    número
  }
```

**S22. Color** (entities and relations): `Entity Cliente [color: #3a83c9]`.

---

## Part C: Relations

**S11. Relation:**

```
Relation compra {
  Cliente (0,n)
  Producto (0,n)
  fecha            // an attribute of the relation
}
```

**S12. How a line inside a relation is read:**

- It's a **participant** when it has a cardinality, a role or `[arrow]`, or simply names an entity or aggregation.
- Anything else is an **attribute** of the relation.
- Write `attr name` to force an attribute, even when the name matches an entity.

**S13. Cardinality `(min,max)`:**

- `min` is a number.
- `max` is a number, `n`, `m` or `*`.
- `(1:n)` also works.
- Cardinality is optional.

**S14. Ratio label.** `1:1`, `1:N`, `N:M` or `1:N:N` (three or more participants) is computed from the max values. You never type it.

**S15. Roles.** An entity related to itself is drawn as a loop:

```
Relation supervisa {
  Empleado (0,1) as jefe
  Empleado (0,n) as subordinado
}
```

**S16. Identifying marks:**

- `[identifying]` draws a double diamond.
- `[id]` draws the "I" bar at the top of the diamond.
- You can use both.

**S24. Arrows.** `Alumnos (1,n) [arrow]` draws an arrowhead at the entity end.

**S17. Missing entities.** If a relation or hierarchy names an entity that doesn't exist, it's **created** (empty) when you paste or leave the editor, with a note such as "Created the missing entity Factura". While you type, it shows as an error instead, so half-typed names don't turn into entities.

---

## Part D: Extended ER

**S18. Hierarchy / generalization** (the "ES UN" triangle):

```
Isa Empleado (1,1) [exclusive, total, by: tipo] {
  Astronauta
  Técnico (0,1)
  Científico
}
```

| Part                            | Meaning                                     | Drawn as                                   |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `[exclusive]` / `[overlapping]` | Exclusiva / solapada (default: overlapping) | Arc under the triangle, or none            |
| `[total]` / `[partial]`         | Total / parcial (default: partial)          | Small circle on the parent's line, or none |
| `[by: tipo]`                    | Discriminator attribute                     | Attribute on the triangle                  |
| `Isa Parent (1,1)` (S23)        | Parent cardinality (optional)               | Label on the parent's line                 |
| `Child (0,1)`                   | Child cardinality (optional)                | Label on the child's line                  |

- Children that don't exist yet are created (S17). Give them attributes with their own `Entity Técnico { … }`.
- **Inline form:** `Entity Técnico [isa: Empleado] { … }` adds Técnico to Empleado's hierarchy.
- **S25. Chained hierarchies** work: a child can be the parent of another `Isa`.

**S19. Aggregation.** A box around a relation and its entities, which then takes part in other relations like an entity. The first line is the relation; the rest are the aggregation's own attributes.

```
Relation esta_casado_con {
  Hombre (1,1)
  Mujer (1,1)
}

Aggregate Matrimonio { esta_casado_con
  fecha_boda
}

Relation reside_en {
  Matrimonio (0,n)
  Dirección (1,1)
}
```

- Dragging the box moves everything inside it.
- Deleting the box keeps its contents.

**S20. Constraints between relations:**

```
Constraint exclusive Empleado: asignado, pertenece        // exclusividad: only one of them (arc)
Constraint inclusive Empleado (2,n): asiste -> diseña     // inclusividad: diseña needs asiste 2+ times
Constraint exclusion: diseña, fabrica                     // exclusión: not both (line between diamonds)
Constraint inclusion: se_casa -> se_divorcia              // inclusión: se_divorcia needs se_casa (arrow)
```

- `->` points from the requirement to the relation that needs it.
- Naming an unknown relation is an error.
- Removing a relation removes its constraints.

---

## Part E: Look

**S21. Attribute style.** Attributes are drawn as Chen ellipses by default. Switch to **lollipop** circles (keys filled black) with the panel button, or with this line at the top of the text:

```
Diagram [style: lollipop]
```

**S26. Diagram name.** The same line can name the diagram; the name shows in the panel header and its list of diagrams:

```
Diagram Ventas [style: lollipop]
```

When a shape is selected, the Text tab scrolls to its block and highlights it (an attribute highlights its owner's block).

---

## Part F: Full examples

### Actividad 11 (basic)

```
Entity Cliente {
  *dni
  nombre
  apellidos
  fecha_nac
  tfno
}

Entity Producto {
  *código
  nombre
  precio
}

Entity Proveedor {
  *nif
  nombre
  dirección
}

Relation compra {
  Cliente (0,n)
  Producto (0,n)
}

Relation suministra {
  Proveedor (1,1)
  Producto (1,n)
}
```

### Actividad 31: Star Trek (hierarchy)

```
Entity Personaje {
  *código
  nombre
  grado
}

Isa Personaje [exclusive, total, by: raza] {
  Humano
  Klingon
  Vulcano
}

Entity Humano {
  ciudad
  f_nacim
}

Entity Klingon {
  planeta
  f_ult_combate
}

Entity Vulcano {
  mentor
  fecha_grado
}
```

### Actividad 38: ONG Reyes Magos (weak entity, "I" mark, derived, loop)

```
Entity Vecino {
  *dni
  nombre
  apellidos
  rey_mago
}

Entity GrupoVecinos {
  *nombre
  barrio
  /n_integrantes
}

Entity Eventos [weak] {
  ~fecha_hora
  ubicación
}

Entity Niño {
  *código
  nombre
  dirección
}

Relation convence {
  Vecino (1,1) as captador
  Vecino (1,n) as convencido
}

Relation pertenece {
  Vecino (1,n)
  GrupoVecinos (1,1)
}

Relation organiza [id] {
  GrupoVecinos (1,1)
  Eventos (0,n)
}

Relation acude {
  Niño (1,n)
  Eventos (0,1)
}
```

### Actividad 37: Videoteca (aggregation, hierarchy, lollipop)

```
Diagram [style: lollipop]

Entity Socios {
  *num_soc
  nombre
  dirección
  dni [optional]
}

Entity Productos {
  *id_prod
  título
  num_copia
}

Entity Empleados {
  *dni
  nombre
  tfno
  dirección
}

Relation tiene_en_prestamo {
  Socios (1,n) [arrow]
  Productos (0,n) [arrow]
}

Aggregate Prestado { tiene_en_prestamo }

Relation préstamo {
  Prestado (0,n) [arrow]
  Empleados (1,1)
  fech_pres
  fech_dev
}

Isa Productos [exclusive, by: tipo_producto] {
  Discos
  Vídeos
}

Entity Discos {
  discografía
  autores
}

Entity Vídeos {
  protagonista
  duración
  director
}
```

### Constraints (slide 112)

```
Relation asignado {
  Empleado (0,1)
  GrupoPracticas (0,n)
}

Relation pertenece {
  Empleado (0,1)
  Departamento (0,n)
}

Relation asiste {
  Empleado (0,n)
  Curso (0,n)
}

Relation diseña {
  Empleado (0,n)
  Producto (0,n)
}

Relation fabrica {
  Empleado (0,n)
  Producto (0,n)
}

Constraint exclusive Empleado: asignado, pertenece
Constraint inclusive Empleado (2,n): asiste -> diseña
Constraint exclusion: diseña, fabrica
```

---

## Visual editor reference

The **Visual** tab shows a form for the selected shape. Every change is one undo step, and new shapes are placed for you.

| Selected    | Form                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Entity      | Name, **Weak**, outline color, attributes, "Used in" (click to jump), **Add hierarchy**                                                                        |
| Attribute   | Name and the PK / PK~ / Multi / Derived / Opt toggles; ↑ ↓ to reorder; "Add a part" makes it composite; a button to edit its owner                             |
| Relation    | Name, **Identifying**, **I mark**, the computed ratio; participants (entity or aggregation, `(min,max)`, role, **Arrow**); attributes; **Make an aggregation** |
| Hierarchy   | Parent and its cardinality, Overlapping/Exclusive, Partial/Total, discriminator, children (pick existing or **New entity**)                                    |
| Aggregation | Name, the relation it groups, its attributes                                                                                                                   |
| Constraint  | Kind, entity (for exclusividad/inclusividad), the two relations (with a swap button), how many times (inclusividad)                                            |

</file>

[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=Cloudy Canvas
Comment=Boards and designs on one canvas
Exec=cloudy-canvas %F
Icon=cloudy-canvas
StartupWMClass=cloudy-canvas

<file path="packaging/arch/PKGBUILD">
# Local pacman package for Arch-based systems (Arch, CachyOS, …).
# Packages the binary built by `tauri build --no-bundle`; run `pnpm release:arch`
# from the repo root, then `sudo pacman -U packaging/arch/cloudy-canvas-*.pkg.tar.zst`.

_root="$startdir/../.."
_tauri="$_root/src-tauri"

pkgname=cloudy-canvas
pkgver=$(sed -n 's/^ "version": "\(.*\)",$/\1/p' "$_tauri/tauri.conf.json")
pkgrel=1
pkgdesc="Cloudy Canvas — boards and designs on one canvas"
arch=('x86_64')
url="https://github.com/Cloudy-Studio-Apps/cloudy-canvas"
license=('AGPL-3.0-only')
depends=('webkit2gtk-4.1' 'gtk3' 'libsoup3' 'hicolor-icon-theme')
options=('!strip' '!debug')

package() {
install -Dm755 "$_tauri/target/release/cloudy-canvas" "$pkgdir/usr/bin/cloudy-canvas"

install -Dm644 "$startdir/cloudy-canvas.desktop" "$pkgdir/usr/share/applications/cloudy-canvas.desktop"
install -Dm644 "$startdir/cloudy-canvas.xml" "$pkgdir/usr/share/mime/packages/cloudy-canvas.xml"

local icons="$_tauri/icons" share="$pkgdir/usr/share/icons/hicolor"
install -Dm644 "$icons/32x32.png" "$share/32x32/apps/cloudy-canvas.png"
install -Dm644 "$icons/64x64.png" "$share/64x64/apps/cloudy-canvas.png"
install -Dm644 "$icons/128x128.png" "$share/128x128/apps/cloudy-canvas.png"
install -Dm644 "$icons/128x128@2x.png" "$share/256x256/apps/cloudy-canvas.png"
install -Dm644 "$icons/icon.png" "$share/512x512/apps/cloudy-canvas.png"
install -Dm644 "$icons/source/app-icon.svg" "$share/scalable/apps/cloudy-canvas.svg"

# The board and design files use the app icon too.

local size type
for size in 32x32 64x64 128x128 256x256 512x512; do
install -d "$share/$size/mimetypes"
for type in board design; do
ln -s ../apps/cloudy-canvas.png "$share/$size/mimetypes/application-x-cloudy-canvas-$type.png"
done
done
}
</file>

// Paths: outlines made of cubic curves (`PathShape`), and what's done with them: booleans and

// stroke outlines, bounds, hit tests, placement and drawing with real holes.

<file path="src/canvas/path/path.types.ts">
import type { Point } from "../geometry.types";
⋮----
/** A cubic bezier's four control points. */
export type CubicCurve = readonly [Point, Point, Point, Point];
⋮----
/** One piece of a contour: a cubic bezier from where the previous one ended (straight when its
 * control points lie on its ends). */
export interface PathSegment {
  c1: Point;
  c2: Point;
  to: Point;
}
⋮----
/**
 * A run of segments from `start`. A closed contour's last segment ends back at `start`. In a
 * normalized shape (see `normalizePath`), each outer contour is followed by its holes.
 */
export interface PathContour {
  start: Point;
  segments: PathSegment[];
  closed: boolean;
  /** A hole of the outer contour before it (normalized shapes only). */
  hole?: boolean;
}
⋮----
/** A hole of the outer contour before it (normalized shapes only). */
⋮----
/** An outline made of contours: what's filled, stroked, clipped or combined. */
export interface PathShape {
  contours: PathContour[];
}
⋮----
/** Which parts of overlapping or self-crossing contours are inside. */
export type PathFillRule = "nonzero" | "evenodd";
⋮----
/** How booleans combine their operands, as in Figma. */
export type PathOperation = "union" | "subtract" | "intersect" | "exclude";
⋮----
/** A shape that takes part in a boolean, filled by its own rule. */
export interface PathOperand {
  shape: PathShape;
  fillRule: PathFillRule;
}
⋮----
/** How a stroke is turned into the area it covers (`outlineStroke`). */
export interface StrokeOutlineOptions {
  width: number;
  cap?: "butt" | "round" | "square";
  join?: "miter" | "round" | "bevel";
  /** Miters longer than this many times the half width are beveled (default 4, as in Figma). */
  miterLimit?: number;
}
⋮----
/** Miters longer than this many times the half width are beveled (default 4, as in Figma). */
⋮----
/** Where a stroke sits on a closed outline: within it, centered on it or around it. */
export type StrokeAlign = "inside" | "center" | "outside";
⋮----
/** How a stroke's area is worked out (`strokeArea`): its outline, alignment and dashes. */
export interface StrokeAreaOptions extends StrokeOutlineOptions {
  /** Default: centered. */
  align?: StrokeAlign;
  /** Dash, gap, dash, gap… lengths (see `dashPath`); empty for a solid stroke. */
  dashes?: readonly number[];
  /** How far along each contour the pattern starts. */
  dashOffset?: number;
}
⋮----
/** Default: centered. */
⋮----
/** Dash, gap, dash, gap… lengths (see `dashPath`); empty for a solid stroke. */
⋮----
/** How far along each contour the pattern starts. */
⋮----
/** A value per side of a box (e.g. individual stroke weights). */
export interface BoxSides {
  top: number;
  right: number;
  bottom: number;
  left: number;
}
⋮----
/** A shape's placement: its top-left corner and its turn (degrees counterclockwise round it). */
export interface PathPlacement {
  x: number;
  y: number;
  rotation?: number;
}
⋮----
/** An axis-aligned box as its edges. */
export interface Extent {
  minX: number;
  minY: number;
  maxX: number;
  maxY: number;
}
⋮----
/** Where a flattened point lies on a source curve (see `SourceTags`). */
export interface CurveTag {
  curve: CubicCurve;
  t: number;
}
⋮----
/** A stretch of a source curve an output edge follows (rebuilding curves). */
export interface CurveRun {
  curve: CubicCurve;
  t0: number;
  t1: number;
}
</file>

<file path="src/products/board/modules/table/table.types.ts">
import type { CanvasElement, ElementDefaults, Size } from "@canvas";
⋮----
import type { TableCell } from "./table.layout.types";
⋮----
/**
 * A grid of text cells. Column widths and row heights are stored; the bounds are their sums. Rows
 * grow to fit their text, so they're never shorter than what's written in them.
 */
export interface TableElement extends CanvasElement {
  type: "table";
  /** Column widths, left to right. */
  columns: number[];
  /** Row heights, top to bottom. */
  rows: number[];
  /** Cell texts, `cells[row][column]`. */
  cells: string[][];
  /** Cell background colors, `fills[row][column]`; `""` is the default (white, or the header tint). */
  fills: string[][];
  /** Whether the first row is a bold, tinted header. */
  header: boolean;
  /** The header row's tint. */
  color: string;
  /**
   * How much its text and cell insets are grown or shrunk (the Scale tool); unset is 1.
   */
  textScale?: number;
}
⋮----
/** Column widths, left to right. */
⋮----
/** Row heights, top to bottom. */
⋮----
/** Cell texts, `cells[row][column]`. */
⋮----
/** Cell background colors, `fills[row][column]`; `""` is the default (white, or the header tint). */
⋮----
/** Whether the first row is a bold, tinted header. */
⋮----
/** The header row's tint. */
⋮----
/**
   * How much its text and cell insets are grown or shrunk (the Scale tool); unset is 1.
   */
⋮----
export interface TableDefaults extends ElementDefaults {
  size: Size;
  fontSize: number;
  /** A new table's grid. */
  columnCount: number;
  rowCount: number;
  columnWidth: number;
  rowHeight: number;
  /** Text inset inside a cell. */
  padX: number;
  padY: number;
  minColumnWidth: number;
  minRowHeight: number;
  /** Thickness of the "+" strips beside a selected table, and their gap to it (screen px). */
  addBarPx: number;
  addGapPx: number;
  /** Row and column grips: their distance outside the table, length and thickness (screen px). */
  gripOffsetPx: number;
  gripLengthPx: number;
  gripThicknessPx: number;
  /** How close to a grid line counts as grabbing it (screen px). */
  lineReachPx: number;
}
⋮----
/** A new table's grid. */
⋮----
/** Text inset inside a cell. */
⋮----
/** Thickness of the "+" strips beside a selected table, and their gap to it (screen px). */
⋮----
/** Row and column grips: their distance outside the table, length and thickness (screen px). */
⋮----
/** How close to a grid line counts as grabbing it (screen px). */
⋮----
/**
 * A part of a table: some cells (one is edited in place; several are picked with Shift or
 * Ctrl/Cmd), or a whole row or column (selected by its grip).
 */
export type TablePart =
  | { kind: "cells"; cells: TableCell[] }
  | { kind: "row"; index: number }
  | { kind: "column"; index: number };
⋮----
/** Which way a grid line or a grip runs: `column` lines are vertical, `row` lines horizontal. */
export type TableAxis = "row" | "column";
</file>

import type {
  ElementDefaults,
  FontStyle,
  FontWeight,
  TextAlign,
  TextDecoration,
  TextRun,
} from "@canvas";
⋮----
import type { DesignNode, Paint } from "../core";
⋮----
/**
 * How a text box follows its text: `width` grows both ways and never wraps, `height` keeps its
 * width and grows down, `none` keeps its size (Figma's auto width, auto height and fixed size).
 */
export type TextAutoResize = "width" | "height" | "none";
⋮----
/** Where the text block sits in a box taller than it. */
export type TextVerticalAlign = "top" | "middle" | "bottom";
⋮----
/**
 * What a range of a text sets over the text's own typography and look (Figma's mixed styles):
 * fields left out are the text's.
 */
export interface TextRunStyle {
  fontFamily?: string;
  fontSize?: number;
  fontWeight?: FontWeight;
  fontStyle?: FontStyle;
  lineHeight?: number;
  letterSpacing?: number;
  /** Its paints; the first visible solid one colors its characters. */
  fills?: Paint[];
  textDecoration?: TextDecoration;
}
⋮----
/** Its paints; the first visible solid one colors its characters. */
⋮----
/** A styled range of a text. */
export type TextNodeRun = TextRun<TextRunStyle>;
⋮----
/**
 * A text layer. Its color is its first visible solid fill; `runs` style ranges of it their own
 * way (mixed fonts, sizes, colors, decorations).
 */
export interface TextNodeElement extends DesignNode {
  type: "text";
  text: string;
  /** A family name, e.g. "Roboto" (installed or from Google Fonts). */
  fontFamily: string;
  fontSize: number;
  fontWeight: FontWeight;
  fontStyle: FontStyle;
  /** Line height as a multiple of the font size. */
  lineHeight: number;
  /** Extra space between characters, in world units. */
  letterSpacing: number;
  textAlign: TextAlign;
  verticalAlign: TextVerticalAlign;
  autoResize: TextAutoResize;
  /** Underline or strikethrough for all of it (runs may set their own). */
  textDecoration: TextDecoration;
  /** Ranges styled their own way, sorted, without overlaps (`normalizeRuns`). */
  runs: TextNodeRun[];
}
⋮----
/** A family name, e.g. "Roboto" (installed or from Google Fonts). */
⋮----
/** Line height as a multiple of the font size. */
⋮----
/** Extra space between characters, in world units. */
⋮----
/** Underline or strikethrough for all of it (runs may set their own). */
⋮----
/** Ranges styled their own way, sorted, without overlaps (`normalizeRuns`). */
⋮----
/** The typography fields of a text, what the Typography section edits. */
export type TextTypography = Pick<
  TextNodeElement,
  "fontFamily" | "fontSize" | "fontWeight" | "fontStyle" | "lineHeight" | "letterSpacing"
>;

 * (closing a loop fills it). Esc lets go of the end.

/**
 * A place features plug into (the toolbar, the canvas's element kinds, the agent tools, …), as a
 * typed token. The code that reads a point defines and exports it; modules contribute to it.
 * `T` is what's contributed.
 */
export interface ExtensionPoint<T> {
  /** Unique, e.g. `"board.toolbar"`; used in error messages. */
  readonly id: string;
  /**
   * Key of an item. Keyed points take one item per key (a second one throws, so two modules can't
   * silently collide); the others are plain ordered lists.
   */
  readonly keyOf?: (item: T) => string;
}

}
⋮----
/** What a module's `register` contributes through; read by the code that owns each point. */
export interface ModuleHost {
  /** Adds items to a point. Only allowed while the modules register. */
  contribute<T>(point: ExtensionPoint<T>, ...items: NoInfer<T>[]): void;
  /** Everything contributed to the point, in module order (then contribution order). */
  get<T>(point: ExtensionPoint<T>): readonly T[];
  /** The item with this key on a keyed point. */
  find<T>(point: ExtensionPoint<T>, key: string): T | undefined;
  /** The id of the module that contributed the item with this key on a keyed point. */
  ownerOf<T>(point: ExtensionPoint<T>, key: string): string | undefined;
  /** Whether a module with this id is loaded. */
  has(moduleId: string): boolean;
}

<file path="index.html">
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/favicon.svg" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>Cloudy Canvas</title>
    <script>
      // Apply the persisted theme before first paint to avoid a flash. Key and flag match shared/stores/theme-store.ts.
      var FORCE_LIGHT_THEME = true;
      try {
        var stored = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("cloudy-canvas:theme") || "{}");
        var pref = FORCE_LIGHT_THEME
          ? "light"
          : (stored.state && stored.state.preference) || "system";
        var dark =
          pref === "dark" ||
          (pref === "system" && matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches);
        document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", dark);
      } catch (_) {}
    </script>
  </head>

  <body>
    <div id="root"></div>
    <script type="module" src="/src/app/main.tsx"></script>
  </body>
</html>
</file>

import type { CanvasDocument } from "../document";
import type { Rect } from "../geometry.types";
import type { SnapAxis } from "../snapping";
⋮----
/**
 * A line dragged out of a ruler, that things snap to. On `x` it's a vertical line (dragged out of
 * the left ruler), on `y` a horizontal one (out of the top ruler). A page guide crosses the whole
 * canvas at `value`; a frame's guide (`frame`, the element it belongs to) shows only inside that
 * element, `value` from its top-left corner, and moves with it.
 */
export interface RulerGuide {
  axis: SnapAxis;
  value: number;
  frame?: string;
}
⋮----
/**
 * A guide where it shows: its world `value` and, for a frame's guide, the area it's drawn in. A
 * turned frame's guide turns with it: `value` and `within` are then in the frame's unturned
 * frame, turned by `rotation` round `within`'s corner.
 */
export interface PlacedGuide {
  /** Its index in the scope's list. */
  index: number;
  axis: SnapAxis;
  /** World units (in the frame's unturned frame when it's turned). */
  value: number;
  /** The frame it belongs to, if any. */
  frame: string | null;
  /** Where it shows: the frame's (unturned) bounds, or `null` across the whole canvas. */
  within: Rect | null;
  /** The frame's turn (degrees counterclockwise round `within`'s corner); 0 for page guides. */
  rotation: number;
}
⋮----
/** Its index in the scope's list. */
⋮----
/** World units (in the frame's unturned frame when it's turned). */
⋮----
/** The frame it belongs to, if any. */
⋮----
/** Where it shows: the frame's (unturned) bounds, or `null` across the whole canvas. */
⋮----
/** The frame's turn (degrees counterclockwise round `within`'s corner); 0 for page guides. */
⋮----
/**
 * Where a product keeps its ruler guides (one module at most): a list per scope (a design's page),
 * stored in the document so they're saved and undoable. Without it, the canvas has no guides.
 */
export interface CanvasGuides {
  /** The guides of `scope` (`null`: a product without scopes). */
  read(doc: CanvasDocument, scope: string | null): RulerGuide[];
  /** Replaces the guides of `scope`, in the current undo step. */
  write(doc: CanvasDocument, scope: string | null, guides: readonly RulerGuide[]): void;
}
⋮----

<file path="src/products/design/modules/core/network/network.types.ts">
import type { CubicCurve, Point } from "@canvas";
⋮----
/**
 * A curve between two vertices: a cubic bezier whose control points are the vertices plus their
 * tangents (relative; `{ x: 0, y: 0 }` is a straight end), as in Figma's vector networks.
 */
export interface VectorSegment {
  start: number;
  end: number;
  tangentStart: Point;
  tangentEnd: Point;
}
⋮----
/** How a region with several loops is filled (holes are drawn filled for now). */
export type WindingRule = "nonzero" | "evenodd";
⋮----
/** A filled area: closed loops of segment indices (the first is its outline). */
export interface VectorRegion {
  loops: number[][];
  windingRule: WindingRule;
}
⋮----
/**
 * Figma's vector network: vertices (local coordinates) joined by bezier segments that may
 * branch, and the regions they close that are filled. Stored as plain JSON in the node.
 */
export interface VectorNetwork {
  vertices: Point[];
  segments: VectorSegment[];
  regions: VectorRegion[];
}
⋮----
/** Where a point lies near a segment: its index, the curve parameter and the distance. */
export interface SegmentHit {
  segment: number;
  t: number;
  distance: number;
}
⋮----
/** An area the segments enclose: its loop of segments (in order) and its flattened outline. */
export interface NetworkFace {
  loop: number[];
  polygon: Point[];
  /** Its area (positive). */
  area: number;
}
⋮----
/** Its area (positive). */
⋮----
/** A segment walked one way: `forward` from its start to its end (finding faces). */
export interface HalfEdge {
  segment: number;
  forward: boolean;
}
⋮----
/** Curves that follow each other, as strokes trace them (`strokeChains`). */
export interface NetworkChain {
  curves: CubicCurve[];
  closed: boolean;
}
</file>

 * (desktop: Tauri's clipboard manager; elsewhere: `navigator.clipboard`).
 */
export interface Clipboard {
  writeText(text: string): Promise<void>;
  /** The clipboard's text, or `null` when it holds none. */
  readText(): Promise<string | null>;
  /** The clipboard's image as an encoded file (e.g. PNG), or `null` when it holds none. */
  readImage(): Promise<Blob | null>;
  /** Puts a PNG file on the clipboard as an image. */
  writeImage(png: Blob): Promise<void>;
}

<file path="docs/board-roadmap.md">
# Board roadmap

What's still missing for the board to feel like FigJam, roughly ordered by value.

**Already on the board:** stickies, text, drawing (pen, highlighter, smoothing, eraser), connectors, geo shapes, sections, tables, images, embeds, stickers, DB tables and enums, ER diagrams.

**Suggested next:** code block, a small, self-contained element folder that fits an existing base. Mind maps would be the next big feature after it.

## High value

- [ ] **Code block**: a monospace box with a language label and syntax highlighting.
  - A `TextBoxKind` with a `language` field; highlighting drawn as colored text runs.
- [ ] **Lists and checklists** in text and stickies: bullets, numbering, checkboxes you can click.
  - Mostly text layout, plus an `interactionAt` press for the checkbox.
- [ ] **Comments**: a pin with a thread.
  - Kept in the doc but outside the undo history (like `noteHidden`, with `doc.updateUntracked`).
  - Matters most once collaboration arrives; a local version is still useful.

## Medium value

- [ ] **Mind map**: a tree of nodes that lays itself out; Tab adds a child, Enter a sibling.
  - A derived-geometry family through `resolveElements`, like the ER auto-layout (`er/layout/`).
- [ ] **Washi tape**: a decorative translucent strip with patterns.
  - A `LineKind` with a fixed thickness and pattern fills.
- [ ] **More link card providers**: GitHub, Figma, Google Docs, Loom.
  - Extend `fetchLinkPreview` (`shared/core/links/`) and the embed `provider`.
- [ ] **Charts**: a small bar, line or pie chart.
  - Fed from a table element as its data source.
- [ ] **Lasso select**: freeform area selection.
  - A select-tool mode, not a new element.

## Widgets (interactive, for facilitating sessions)

- [ ] **Voting session**: each person gets N dots to place on stickies; the board shows a tally.
  - Builds on stickers.
- [ ] **Timer**: a board-level countdown.
  - Shown in the top bar, not drawn on the canvas.
- [ ] **Poll / counter**: small interactive cards.
  - Same `ctx.activate` action pattern as embeds.

## Productivity features (not elements)

- [ ] **Templates**: retro, kanban, flowchart, user journey.
  - Stored as sections plus stickies, inserted with `insertCopies`.
- [ ] **Tidy up**: arrange the selected stickies in a grid.
- [ ] **Sort and cluster**: sort stickies by color or author; group the selection by color into sections.
- [ ] **Align and distribute** the selection, plus smart guides while dragging.
- [ ] **Locking**: a `locked` flag the select tool respects, so backgrounds and templates can't be moved by accident.
- [ ] **Grouping**: Ctrl+G groups, without sections.
</file>

<file path="src/canvas/elements/element.types.ts">
/**
 * What every element on the canvas is. Elements are plain data (they live in the Yjs doc); their
 * behavior lives in the `ElementKind` registered for their `type`. The set of types is open:
 * built-ins and plugins register kinds at runtime, so code outside an element's folder never
 * assumes which types exist.
 */
export interface CanvasElement {
  id: string;
  /** Key of the element's kind in the registry, e.g. `"sticky"`. */
  type: string;
  /** Fractional index (fractional-indexing): lexicographic order is z-order. */
  index: string;
  /** Top-left corner in world coordinates. */
  x: number;
  y: number;
  w: number;
  h: number;
  /**
   * Locked elements stay where they are: clicks, hover and marquees pass through them, so they
   * can only be selected from the context menu (to unlock them).
   */
  locked?: boolean;
  /**
   * Degrees the element is turned by (counterclockwise, Figma's way) around its top-left corner
   * (x, y); `w`×`h` is its size unturned. Only kinds that are `rotatable` set it.
   */
  rotation?: number;
}
⋮----

⋮----

/**
 * Changes to an element's fields (id and type are immutable). Kinds type them for their element
 * (`ElementPatch<StickyElement>`); the document takes any of them as the base `ElementPatch`.
 */
export type ElementPatch<E extends CanvasElement = CanvasElement> = Partial<Omit<E, "id" | "type">>;
⋮----
/**
 * An element's look, as Copy properties takes it (`ElementKind.styleOf`): stored fields by name,
 * plain JSON, pasted onto any element whose kind has fields of the same names.
 */
export type ElementStyle = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;

import type { BlendMode, CanvasEffect } from "../effects";

⋮----
/** An element's drawing order key: views are stacked by these, compared as strings. */
export type OrderKeyOf = (el: CanvasElement, kind: ElementKind) => string;
⋮----
/**
 * The world area an element is drawn and hit in, when something clips it (e.g. a frame that
 * clips its content): a rect, with rounded corners of `radius`, turned by `rotation` degrees
 * around its top-left corner (a turned frame's).
 */
export interface ElementClip {
  rect: Rect;
  radius: number;
  rotation?: number;
}
⋮----
/** An element's clip, or `null` when nothing clips it. */
export type ClipOf = (el: CanvasElement) => ElementClip | null;
⋮----
/**
 * How a mask shapes what it masks: by its pixels' opacity (`alpha`), by its outline alone, fully
 * opaque wherever it has a shape (`vector`), or by its pixels' brightness (`luminance`).
 */
export type MaskMode = "alpha" | "vector" | "luminance";
⋮----
/** Where an element is drawn under a mask: as part of the mask itself, or masked by it. */
export interface MaskSlot {
  mask: string;
  role: "source" | "masked";
}
⋮----
/** Where an element is drawn inside an element's effects (it, or something it holds). */
export interface EffectSlot {
  /** The element whose effects the scope applies. */
  effect: string;
}
⋮----
/** The element whose effects the scope applies. */
⋮----
/**
 * The innermost container an element is drawn in: a mask's scope or an effect scope. Scopes nest
 * (a masked group with a shadow, a shadowed layer under a mask), each with its own `home`.
 */
export type ScopeSlot = MaskSlot | EffectSlot;
⋮----
/** One outline of a vector mask, in its element's own frame (see `ElementMask.shape`). */
export interface MaskShape {
  /** The element's top-left corner, in world units. */
  x: number;
  y: number;
  /** Degrees counterclockwise round (x, y). */
  rotation: number;
  /** What it covers, in local coordinates (holes stay open). */
  path: PathShape;
}
⋮----
/** The element's top-left corner, in world units. */
⋮----
/** Degrees counterclockwise round (x, y). */
⋮----
/** What it covers, in local coordinates (holes stay open). */
⋮----
/**
 * An element that masks others: they show only where it does (or, `inverted`, only where it
 * doesn't). The mask isn't drawn itself; with what it holds (its `source` slot) it shapes the mask.
 */
export interface ElementMask {

  home: ScopeSlot | null;

  bounds: Rect;
  /**
   * Its outlines, for a `vector` mask (drawn crisp, as a stencil); `null` when some part of it has
   * no outline (a text), which then masks by its pixels made fully opaque.

  shape: readonly MaskShape[] | null;

}

/** The mask element. */
⋮----

⋮----
/** The masks of a canvas, and where each element under one is drawn. */
export interface ElementMasks {
  masks: ReadonlyMap<string, ElementMask>;

}
⋮----
/** Elements under a mask → their innermost slot; elements left out are under none. */
⋮----
/**
 * An element's effects and where they're drawn: over the element's view and the views of what it
 * holds, composited together (a group's shadow is its layers' shadow, as in Figma).
 */
export interface EffectScope {
  /** The element. */
  id: string;
  /** Its visible effects, bottom to top. */
  effects: readonly CanvasEffect[];
  /** Where the scope is drawn: inside another scope, or `null` at the top. */
  home: ScopeSlot | null;
  /** The element's own box (unturned; x, y its top-left corner): effects laid on it use it. */
  box: Rect;
  /** Degrees the element is turned by (counterclockwise round its corner): offsets turn with it. */
  rotation: number;
  /** The world area of what the scope holds, effects left out. */
  bounds: Rect;
  /**
   * How the scope's result is laid on what's behind it: a group's opacity, a layer's blend mode.
   * Left out, it's drawn as it is.
   */
  composite?: ScopeComposite;
}

/** The element. */

/** Degrees the element is turned by (counterclockwise round its corner): offsets turn with it. */

/** The world area of what the scope holds, effects left out. */
⋮----
/**
   * How the scope's result is laid on what's behind it: a group's opacity, a layer's blend mode.
   * Left out, it's drawn as it is.
   */
⋮----
/**
 * The opacity and blend mode a scope's result is composited with (after its effects). An
 * `isolated` scope is drawn on its own first, then composited (what it holds overlaps, or it

 */
export interface ScopeComposite {
  opacity: number;
  blendMode: BlendMode;

}
⋮----
/**

  effectRenderers: EffectRenderers;

  drawn: (el: CanvasElement) => boolean;
}

<file path="src/shared/core/storage.types.ts">
import type { FileInfo, FileMeta, FileType } from "./files.types";
⋮----
/**
 * Platform-agnostic persistence. Implemented per platform in `platform/`
 * (desktop: Tauri filesystem; later: web/IndexedDB, remote backend).
 * Files are addressed by a stable id; the platform keeps track of where each one lives.
 */
export interface Storage {
  /** Recently opened or saved files, newest first. */
  list(): Promise<FileInfo[]>;
  get(id: string): Promise<FileInfo | null>;
  /** Whether the file with this id is still where it was last seen. */
  exists(id: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Records an existing file (e.g. picked in the open dialog), reusing its id when it's known. */
  register(path: string): Promise<FileInfo>;
  /** Points a known file at its new location (it was moved), keeping its id. */
  relocate(id: string, path: string): Promise<FileInfo>;
  /**
   * Removes a file from the recent files, with its preview picture. The file itself is left
   * alone, unless it's a draft.
   */
  forget(id: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Empties the recent files, except drafts. The files themselves are left alone. */
  clear(): Promise<void>;
  /** Where the recent files list is kept, or `null` where it isn't a file (browser). */
  indexLocation(): Promise<string | null>;
  load(id: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  /**
   * Writes `data` to `path` and records the file under `id`, with its title and description.
   * A draft saved elsewhere is removed.
   */
  save(id: string, path: string, data: Uint8Array, meta?: FileMeta): Promise<FileInfo>;
  /**
   * Autosaves a file that has no location yet as a draft kept by the app, recorded under `id`
   * with `name` (drafts are named by the app, not by their file).
   */
  saveDraft(
    id: string,
    name: string,
    type: FileType,
    data: Uint8Array,
    meta?: FileMeta,
  ): Promise<FileInfo>;
  /** A file's preview picture (an image file), or `null` when it has none. */
  loadThumbnail(id: string): Promise<Uint8Array | null>;
  /** Stores a file's preview picture; `null` removes it (e.g. the canvas is empty). */
  saveThumbnail(id: string, image: Uint8Array | null): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * True once after the recent files had to be reset because they couldn't be read
   * (the unreadable list is kept aside), so the UI can say so.
   */
  takeIndexReset(): boolean;
}
⋮----

/**
 * What dragging a resize handle does: `resize` changes the bounds (text rewraps, strokes keep
 * their weight), `scale` scales the selection and everything in it like a picture (the Scale
 * tool, K; always proportional).

⋮----

}

⋮----
/**

 * around it, which scales every element in it.
 */
export interface ResizeTarget {
  elements: CanvasElement[];
  box: Rect;
  /** Degrees `box` is turned by around its top-left corner (one turned element's). */

}

/** Degrees `box` is turned by around its top-left corner (one turned element's). */

 * every element in it (ones that can't be resized move by their center, with their members). Shift keeps the
 * proportions (always, when a kind keeps them), Alt resizes round the center. A turned element
 * resizes in its own frame, its opposite side staying put. The dragged sides of unturned ones snap
 * to other elements. In `scale` mode (the Scale tool) the proportions are always kept and every
 * element, with what moves with it, is scaled through its kind (`ElementKind.scale`): fonts,
 * strokes and radii grow with it.

/** Figma design files ("Save local copy…"), imported as new designs. */
⋮----
/** FigJam files ("Save local copy…"), imported as new boards. */
⋮----
/** Figma's files the app imports, and what each becomes. */
⋮----
export function isFileType(value: string | undefined): value is FileType
⋮----
/** Image files the app can show, by extension, with their media type. */
⋮----
/** File name without folders, e.g. "/home/me/Plan.cboard" → "Plan.cboard". */
export function baseNameFromPath(path: string): string
⋮----
/** File name without folders or extension, e.g. "/home/me/Plan.cboard" → "Plan". */
export function fileNameFromPath(path: string): string
⋮----
/** The lowercase extension of a file name or path, without the dot; `""` when it has none. */
export function extensionOf(path: string): string
⋮----
/** The media type of an image file by its extension, or `null` when it isn't one. */
export function imageTypeFromName(name: string): string | null
⋮----
/** Appends the file type's extension when the path doesn't already end with it. */
export function withFileExtension(path: string, type: FileType): string
⋮----
/** Returns the file type for a path based on its extension, or `null` if it isn't a Cloudy Canvas file. */
export function fileTypeFromPath(path: string): FileType | null
⋮----
/**
 * What a Figma file at this path is imported as (a `.fig` as a design, a FigJam `.jam` as a
 * board), or `null` when it isn't one.
 */
export function figmaImportOf(path: string): FileType | null
⋮----
/** Whether the app opens this path: one of its own files, or a Figma or FigJam file to import. */
export function isOpenablePath(path: string): boolean
⋮----
/** Whether a value read from disk (e.g. the recent files index) is a well-formed `FileInfo`. */
export function isFileInfo(value: unknown): value is FileInfo
⋮----
/** The name to show for a file: its title, or its file name when it has none. */
export function displayName(file: Pick<FileInfo, "name" | "title">): string
</file>
