<file path="README.md">
<p align="center">
  <img src="src-tauri/icons/source/app-icon.png" alt="Cloudy Canvas" width="112">
</p>

<h1 align="center">Cloudy Canvas</h1>

<p align="center">
  Whiteboards and designs in one desktop app, with your files kept on your own disk.
  <br>
  by <strong>DarkRedgm</strong> · part of <strong>Cloudy Studio</strong>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://github.com/Cloudy-Studio-Apps/cloudy-canvas/releases/latest">Download</a> ·
  <a href="docs/plugins.md">Plugins</a> ·
  <a href="#building-from-source">Build from source</a>
</p>

> **Early demo.** Cloudy Canvas is under heavy development. Expect missing features and rough edges, and keep copies of files that matter to you.

## What it is

One app with two kinds of files on a shared canvas engine:

- **Boards** (`.cboard`), FigJam-style whiteboards with sticky notes, shapes, connectors, text, sections, tables, freehand drawing, stickers, images, link cards, database schemas (DBML) and ER diagrams.
- **Designs** (`.cdesign`), Figma-style design files with pages, frames, a layer tree, rectangles, ellipses, polygons, stars, lines, vectors with a pen tool, text with system and Google fonts, gradients, image fills with cropping, boolean operations, masks, strokes, and effects (shadows, blurs, noise, glass, custom shaders).

Also:

- **Local-first.** Files are plain files on your disk, autosaved as you work. No account is needed.
- **Figma and FigJam import.** Open a `.fig` or `.jam` file ("Save local copy…" in Figma) and it becomes an editable design or board.
- **AI agents.** The app runs a local MCP server, so Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code and other agents can read and edit the open board or design while you watch. Every agent edit is one undo step. Open the **Agents** menu in the top bar to connect one.
- **Plugins.** New element types, tools, panels and agent tools can be added as plugins. See [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md) and [examples/plugins](examples/plugins).
- **Exports.** PNG, JPG, PDF and CSV.

**Roadmap:** the desktop app with local files, then a web version of the same app, then real-time collaboration.

## Download

Get the latest build from [Releases](https://github.com/Cloudy-Studio-Apps/cloudy-canvas/releases/latest):

| Platform             | File                                           | Install                                      |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Windows 10/11        | `Cloudy Canvas_<version>_x64-setup.exe`        | Run it                                       |
| Ubuntu / Debian      | `Cloudy Canvas_<version>_amd64.deb`            | `sudo apt install ./Cloudy*.deb`             |
| Arch Linux / CachyOS | `cloudy-canvas-<version>-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst` | `sudo pacman -U cloudy-canvas-*.pkg.tar.zst` |
| Linux (any distro)   | `Cloudy Canvas_<version>_amd64.AppImage`       | `chmod +x` it, then run it                   |

The Windows and AppImage versions update themselves: when a new version is out, the app offers to install it. The `.deb` and Arch packages tell you about it and open the download page. Click the logo, or open **Settings › About**, to check by hand.

Windows SmartScreen may warn about an unknown publisher because the installer isn't code-signed yet. Choose **More info › Run anyway**.

## Building from source

Built with Tauri 2, React 19, TypeScript, Vite, PixiJS, Yjs, Tailwind CSS v4 and Zustand.

### Prerequisites

On every OS you need [Rust](https://rustup.rs) (stable) and Node.js 20+ with pnpm (`corepack enable`).

**Windows 11:** the [Microsoft C++ Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/) with the _Desktop development with C++_ workload, and the MSVC toolchain (`rustup default stable-msvc`). WebView2 is already installed on Windows 11.

**Arch Linux / CachyOS:**

```sh
sudo pacman -S --needed webkit2gtk-4.1 base-devel curl wget file openssl \
  appmenu-gtk-module libappindicator-gtk3 librsvg xdotool
```

For other systems, see [Tauri's prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/).

### Development

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm tauri dev      # the desktop app
pnpm dev            # the frontend alone in a browser (native dialogs unavailable)
pnpm lint           # ESLint
pnpm typecheck      # TypeScript
pnpm format         # Prettier (format:check to verify)
```

### Release builds

| Command                   | Builds                                                 | Output                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pnpm release:linux`      | An AppImage                                            | `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/`                    |
| `pnpm release:arch`       | A pacman package with the desktop entry and file types | `packaging/arch/`                                              |
| `pnpm release:win`        | A Windows installer, cross-built on Linux              | `src-tauri/target/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/release/bundle/nsis/` |
| `pnpm release`            | The AppImage and the Windows installer                 |                                                                |
| `pnpm release:win:native` | NSIS and MSI installers, run **on Windows**            | `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/`                             |

<details>
<summary>Cross-building the Windows installer on Linux</summary>

`pnpm release:win` uses [`cargo-xwin`](https://github.com/rust-cross/cargo-xwin) and NSIS:

```sh
sudo pacman -S --needed clang lld llvm
paru -S nsis                                # from the AUR (or yay -S nsis)
rustup target add x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
cargo install --locked cargo-xwin
```

The first run downloads the Windows SDK, so it takes a while. Cross-building only makes the NSIS installer; build on Windows for an `.msi`.

</details>

### Project layout

```
src/
  app/        app shell: entry, router, providers, MCP server wiring, plugin loading
  platform/   Tauri implementations of the shared interfaces (storage, dialogs, fonts, …)
  shared/     product-agnostic code: core types and helpers, design system, app stores
  canvas/     the canvas engine every product shares (plain TypeScript, no React)
  canvas-ui/  React pieces every editor shares
  products/
    board/    the board: engine side, modules (one folder per feature) and its editor
    design/   the design: engine side, modules and its editor
  pages/      home, settings, design-system preview
src-tauri/    the Rust desktop shell
```

Every feature is a module that plugs into extension points, the same API plugins use. [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) documents the architecture and conventions in detail.

### Publishing a release

Releases are built by GitHub Actions ([`.github/workflows/release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml)) when a version tag is pushed:

```sh
pnpm release:tag 0.2.0   # writes the version, commits "Release v0.2.0", tags v0.2.0 and pushes
```

The workflow builds the Windows installer, the `.deb`, the AppImage and the Arch package into a **draft** release, with the updater's signatures and `latest.json`. Review the notes and press **Publish**: installed apps then see the update.

One-time setup: create the updater's signing key with `pnpm tauri signer generate -w ~/.tauri/cloudy-canvas.key`, put the public key in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`), and add the private key and its password to the repository's Actions secrets as `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` and `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD`. Keep a backup of the private key: without it, installed copies can't verify new updates.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. Before opening a PR, run `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm format:check`, and follow the conventions in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md).

## License

Copyright © 2026 DarkRedgm.

Cloudy Canvas is free software, licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0](LICENSE). You may use, study, change and share it. If you distribute a modified version, or run one as a service others use over a network, you must publish its source under the same license.

### Third-party content

- Emoji graphics: [Twemoji](https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), © Twitter, Inc. and other contributors, licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
- The [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/) typeface by Rasmus Andersson, licensed under the [SIL Open Font License 1.1](https://openfontlicense.org).
- Icons from [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) (ISC) and [Simple Icons](https://simpleicons.org) (CC0). Brand logos are trademarks of their owners.
- Other dependencies keep their own licenses, listed in `package.json` and `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`.

Figma and FigJam are trademarks of Figma, Inc. Cloudy Canvas is not affiliated with or endorsed by Figma.
</file>

<file path="docs/plans/precision-editing.md">
# Precision editing plan: smart guides, snapping, align & distribute, rotation, rulers

## Context

The Design editor (`/design/:id`) has the core node types, pages, vectors and agent tools, but it is
missing the tools for placing things precisely. Every professional design tool has them, and without
them laying out a UI by hand is slow and inexact. What the code has today:

- **No snapping.** The select tool's move (`canvas/tools/select-tool.ts`) applies the raw pointer delta.
  `ResizeGesture` and `NodeDrawTool` round to whole units only.
- **Resize works on one element only** (`render/overlay-state.ts`: resize handles are drawn only when
  `selected.length === 1`). A multi-selection shows a union outline that can't be resized.
- **No arrow-key nudge** (`input/base-keybindings.ts`).
- **Align covers six directions, with no distribute.** `modules/core/ui/sections/align.ts` lives in the
  Design UI, with no command, shortcut or agent tool.
- **No rotation anywhere.** The Figma import (`figma/convert/fig-matrix.ts`) has to flatten rotated
  nodes because of this.
- **No rulers or ruler guides.**

Goal: precise layout in the Design editor (and the board where it fits), built as engine features
products opt into, following the module and kind architecture in CLAUDE.md.

The first implementation step copies this plan to `docs/plans/precision-editing.md` in the repo.

Scope decisions (assumed; easy to change):

- Snapping, multi-resize, nudge, align & distribute: **engine level**. The Design turns them all on and
  the board turns on nudge, multi-resize and align/distribute (snapping off by default, toggleable).
- Rotation and rulers: **Design only** (engine hooks are generic, but only design kinds use them).

---

## Phase 0: Transform foundations (do first, everything builds on it) — done

1. **Arrow-key nudge.** New commands `nudgeLeft/Right/Up/Down` (Arrow keys; Shift = 10 units) in
   `canvas/commands.ts` + `BASE_KEYBINDINGS`. Moves the selection with `withMembers(…, "move")` and skips
   locked elements. It doesn't call `onMoved`, so a nudge never changes a node's parent (Figma's behavior). Repeated presses within ~1 s join one undo step (checkpoint only
   when the last nudge is older). Tools that own arrows (vector edit) take them via `onCommand`:
   `VectorMoveTool` nudges the selected points.
2. **Multi-selection resize.** A `SelectionTransform` (`canvas/tools/selection-transform.ts`): the
   union box of the selected boxed elements gets the 8 resize handles. Dragging scales every element's
   rect relative to that box (`scaleRectInBox(rect, from, to)` in `geometry.ts`) through
   `kind.resize`, which keeps per-kind rules (text relayout, table grid, `keepsRatio`). `ResizeGesture`
   becomes the single-element case of the same gesture. Alt resizes from the center (single and multi),
   Shift keeps the proportions, as it does now.
3. **Size badge.** While an element or selection is moved or resized, a small `W × H` label shows under
   the selection box (overlay, screen space; the Design shows it always while selected, like Figma).
   Opt in with a product view option `sizeBadge`.

Files: `canvas/tools/select-tool.ts`, `canvas/tools/resize-gesture.ts`, `canvas/render/overlay-state.ts`,
`canvas/render/layers/overlay-layer.ts`, `canvas/commands.ts`, `canvas/input/base-keybindings.ts`,
`canvas/geometry.ts`.

## Phase 1: Snapping and smart guides — done

As built (differences from the plan below): targets are chosen by `ElementKind.snapTarget(el)`
instead of a product hook (hidden design layers and groups aren't targets); the defaults come from
`CanvasViewOptions.snapping`; the toggles are in the shared `ZoomMenu` (both editors), not the main
menu; the pen tool doesn't snap yet; "Snap to guides" comes with the ruler guides (Phase 4).

### Engine (`canvas/snapping/`, new folder)

- `snap.types.ts`: `SnapLine { axis: "x" | "y"; value; from; to; source: id | "grid" | "guide" }`,
  `SnapResult { dx, dy, guides: SnapGuide[] }`, `SnapSettings { objects, pixelGrid, guides }`.
- `snap-targets.ts`: builds the candidate lines once per gesture from the **scene** (resolved
  geometry, current scope, visible and unclipped elements only): each element's left/center/right
  and top/middle/bottom, minus the moved elements and their `withMembers` (so a frame never snaps to its
  own children). Limited to elements whose bounds intersect the viewport, plus the parent container's
  edges and center. Product hook `snapTargets?(el, elements)` in `canvas-product.types.ts` /
  `canvas/modules` points to override (the Design adds the parent frame's padding later; text could add
  baselines).
- `snap-rect.ts`: `snapRect(rect, targets, threshold, handles?)` checks the moving rect's 3 x-lines
  and 3 y-lines against the targets (binary search over sorted values), picks the nearest per axis
  within `threshold = SNAP_PX / zoom` (`SNAP_PX = 6`), and returns the offset plus every line matched at
  that offset (several aligned edges light up at once). For a resize, only the dragged edges snap.
- `equal-spacing.ts`: smart distribution guides. When the moving rect sits between or beside siblings
  on a row/column, it snaps to the gap that repeats an existing gap and returns the spacing marks.
- `pixel-snap.ts`: with `pixelGrid`, round to whole units, as today (Figma's "Snap to pixel grid").
- The pointer's Ctrl/Cmd key **turns snapping off** for the gesture (Figma's behavior).

### Drawing the guides

- `render/layers/snap-layer.ts`: screen space, drawn above the overlay: lines in the accent snap color
  (`--canvas-snap` token, red-pink like Figma), small × marks at matched points, and distance labels
  (pooled text, like the link labels) for equal-spacing gaps.
- `ToolContext.snap(rect, options)` returns `{ rect, guides }` and `ctx.setSnapGuides(guides | null)`;
  cleared on pointer up and on cancel.

### Where it applies

- Select-tool move (on the moved selection's union box), `SelectionTransform` resize, `NodeDrawTool`
  (the drawn box and the first click), `LineTool`/`LineEndDrag` (line ends snap to points and edges),
  the pen tool's new points, the frame preset placement, and pastes are left as they are.
- **Alt hover measurement** (Figma's red distance lines): with a selection and Alt held, hovering
  another node shows the distances between them (or to the parent's edges), drawn by the same layer.
  Implemented in `SelectTool.onHover` via a `measure.ts` helper.

### Settings

- `SnapSettings` in `EngineState.snapping`, set with `engine.setSnapping(patch)`; the product's
  `defaultOptions` gives the initial values and `useSnapSettingsStore` (`shared/stores/`, persisted per
  product) remembers them.
- Design main menu → View: "Snap to objects", "Snap to pixel grid", "Snap to guides" (checkbox items;
  the `mainMenu` point needs a `checked(engine)` field). Board: "Snap to objects" in the zoom menu.

## Phase 2: Align, distribute and tidy up — done

As built: aligning doesn't run `onMoved` (nothing changes parent, like a nudge, as in Figma); tidy
up is Alt+Shift+T (Ctrl+Alt+T opens a terminal on many Linux desktops); the board gets the
context menu's Align submenu and the agent tools, not a panel; tidy up also has agent tools
(`tidy_up_nodes`, `tidy_up_shapes`); no "spacing" field.

- Move the math to the engine: `canvas/arrange/align.ts` (from `modules/core/ui/sections/align.ts`),
  plus `distribute.ts` (equal **spacing** horizontally/vertically, keeping the outermost two in place,
  ordered by position) and `tidy-up.ts` (Figma's Tidy up: snaps a rough grid of nodes into rows and
  columns with the median gap).
- Engine commands `alignLeft…alignBottom`, `distributeHorizontal`, `distributeVertical`, `tidyUp`, all
  moving with `withMembers` in one undo step and running `onMoved`. A single element aligns to its parent
  container (product hook `alignTarget?(el, elements)`; the Design returns the parent frame, the
  board the section it's in).
- Keys (Figma's): Alt+A/D/W/S (left/right/top/bottom), Alt+H/V (centers), Alt+Shift+H/V (distribute),
  Ctrl+Alt+T (tidy up).
- UI: the Position section gets a second row (distribute + tidy up buttons, a "spacing" field when the
  selection is distributed); the selection context menu gets an "Align" submenu; the board gets an
  align toolbar in its selection panel (`selectionPanels`).
- Agent tools: `align_nodes`/`distribute_nodes` (design) and `align_shapes`/`distribute_shapes` (board),
  taking ids and leaving the selection alone, like `reorder_shapes`.

## Phase 3: Rotation (Design) — done

As built: Figma's model, `rotation` round the layer's **top-left corner** (not its center, as first
planned below), counterclockwise. The engine turns any `rotatable` kind (`ElementKind.rotatable`,
`rotate`); kinds draw and hit-test unturned. Lines hold their angle in their ends; groups never
turn themselves. Flips mirror vectors and lines; other shapes land mirrored and turned the other
way (polygons and stars turn half round top to bottom); text and image fills aren't mirrored. A
turned frame inside another clipping frame clips by its own area only. Agents: `rotation` field,
`rotate_nodes`, `flip_nodes`. The Figma import keeps rotations; mirrored or skewed layers are
still straightened or vectorized.

### Data model

- `DesignNode.rotation` (degrees, clockwise, default 0, `fillDefaults`) around the box's **center**;
  `x, y, w, h` stay the unrotated box. Simple to patch and to read for agents and the panel.
- Engine support, generic and opt-in on `ElementKind`:
  - `rotationOf(el): number` (base returns 0).
  - `bounds(el)` stays the **axis-aligned** box (for hits, culling, marquee, exports and snapping);
    add `frameOf(el)` (`{ rect, rotation }`) that the overlay and gestures use.
  - `hitTest` in `DesignNodeKind` maps the point into the node's local frame first
    (`toLocal(p, frame)` in `geometry.ts`), so every kind keeps its unrotated hit test.
- Rendering: `ElementView` sets the container's `pivot`/`rotation` from `rotationOf` (drawers keep
  drawing unrotated). Clipping (`ElementClip`) gains an optional `rotation`, masked with a rotated
  rect.

### Interaction

- **Rotate zone**: just outside each corner handle (12 screen px) with a rotate cursor (custom SVG cursor);
  dragging rotates around the selection center, Shift snaps to 15°. Multiple nodes rotate together
  (their centers orbit the group center).
- **Rotated resize**: `resizeRect` runs in the node's local frame, then the fixed corner is pinned in world
  space (`resizeRotated` in `handles/`).
- Overlay draws the rotated outline and handles (`OverlayState.selectionFrames`).
- **Children**: rotating a frame or group rotates its descendants with it (positions orbit, their
  `rotation` adds), through `withMembers(…, "move")`. Group bounds (`resolveGroups`) use the
  children's rotated corners.
- Vector edit mode, the text editor (CSS `transform: rotate`) and the line ends map through the frame.
- Panel: an angle field in the Layout section, plus "Rotate 90° left/right" and "Flip horizontal/vertical"
  (Shift+H / Shift+V: flips vectors' networks, lines' points and image fills; symmetric shapes only
  mirror their rotation).
- Agents: `rotation` in `create_nodes`/`update_nodes` (patchable field, checked number).
- Figma import: `fig-matrix.ts` reads rotation from the transform matrix instead of flattening.

## Phase 4: Rulers and ruler guides (Design) — done

As built: with a selection in a frame (or a selected top-level frame), the rulers count from its
corner and number only its span, like Figma; the selection's extent is marked with its two
values, hiding numbers under them; the Position section's X/Y count from the layer's frame too
(agents keep world coordinates). Guides are the page's (across the whole page) or a frame's: one
dragged out of the rulers while they measure a frame belongs to it (its value from the frame's
corner, shown only inside it, moving with it, dropped with it; dragged past its edges it becomes
a page guide; a turned frame's guides turn with it and are dragged along its axes, but aren't
snapped to; the rulers measure the page while the frame is turned, but a guide dragged out of
them into it still becomes its guide, along its axis closest to the ruler's). Guides go through a product hook, `guides` (`CanvasGuides`; the design keeps them
on each page's record), so the engine stays product-agnostic. The guide toggle is Shift+;,
"Remove all guides" has no key; the snap toggle lives in the zoom menu, the main menu has Rulers,
Ruler guides and Remove all guides as checkbox items. Guides snap to elements and to other guides
while dragged (Ctrl turns it off). Agents: `list_guides`, `add_guides` (`frame` optional),
`remove_guides`. Figma pages' guides are kept on import. Not done: copying a frame doesn't copy
its guides, locking guides, rulers on the board.

- `CanvasViewOptions.rulers` (Design on); rulers are DOM (`canvas-ui/components/rulers/`): a top and a
  left strip 20 px wide drawn on a `<canvas>`, ticks and numbers chosen by zoom (1/2/5 × 10ⁿ steps),
  following `engine.onViewChange`. The selection's range is highlighted on both, and the origin is the
  page's (0, 0), or the selected top frame's corner like Figma.
- Toggle: Shift+R (`toggleRulers` host command, main menu → View).
- **Ruler guides**: dragging out of a ruler adds a guide; guides are stored on the page record
  (`PageElement.guides: { axis, value }[]`, so they're per page and saved with the file, undoable). A
  guide layer draws them (screen-space lines, the pink snap color); dragging one moves it, dragging it
  back onto the ruler deletes it; the position shows while dragging. They are snap targets (`SnapSettings.guides`).
- "Show/hide guides" and "Remove all guides" in the View menu.

## Phase 5: Other recommended precision features

Ordered by value for the effort:

1. **Zoom to selection** (Shift+2) and **zoom to previous/next frame** (N / Shift+N), engine commands.
   — done. As built: both zoom past 100% like Figma; the frames come from a product hook,
   `frames` (the design's top-level visible frames and sections, the board's sections), in
   reading order; N starts from the selected frame or the one holding the selection, else the one
   nearest the middle of the view. In the zoom menu, the selection's context menu and the design's
   View menu.
2. **Copy/paste properties** (Ctrl+Alt+C / Ctrl+Alt+V: fills, strokes, opacity, radius, text style).
   — done. As built: kinds list their `styleFields` (`styleOf`, `applyStyle`), matched by name
   across types; the copied look is kept per product for the app session, not on the system
   clipboard; both products (board colors, sizes and fonts too); agents use
   `copy_properties_to_nodes` / `copy_properties_to_shapes`.
3. **Select matching layers** (same type and fills) and **select inverse**, in the context menu.
4. **Pixel preview** at high zoom: the pixel grid already exists; add "Snap to pixel grid" rounding to
   rotation-free nodes only.
5. **Layout grids on frames** (columns/rows/grid, drawn over the frame, snap targets): after rotation,
   because grids and snapping share the target code.
6. **Keyboard resize**: Ctrl+Arrow grows/shrinks the selection by 1 (Shift = 10), like Figma.

## Implementation order and size

| Phase                               | Size   | Depends on            |
| ----------------------------------- | ------ | --------------------- |
| 0 Nudge, multi-resize, size badge   | S–M    | —                     |
| 1 Snapping + smart guides + measure | L      | 0                     |
| 2 Align / distribute / tidy up      | M      | 0                     |
| 3 Rotation                          | XL     | 0, 1 (snap uses AABB) |
| 4 Rulers + guides                   | M      | 1                     |
| 5 Extras                            | S each | —                     |

Each phase ships on its own: a commit per phase, CLAUDE.md updated in the same commit (engine
sections + Design section), plus `docs/plugins.md` when a new hook or point is exposed to plugins.

## Reuse

- `canvas/geometry.ts` (`unionRects`, `rectFromPoints`, `roundRect`, `rectCenter`).
- `canvas/handles/resize-handles.ts` (`resizeRect`, `RESIZE_HANDLES`) for multi and rotated resize.
- `ctx.withMembers`, `ctx.moved` / `onMoved` (drops into frames after drags and aligns; nudges keep the parent).
- `ctx.setGuide` / `GuideLayer` pattern and the link layer's pooled labels for distance text.
- `modules/core/ui/sections/align.ts` (moved, not rewritten), `useMoveNodes`.
- `canvas/agent/` (`asUndoStep`, `requireNodes`) for the new agent tools.
- The `mainMenu`, `contextMenu` and `propertySections` points for all UI entry points.

## Verification

- After each step: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm format:check` (the project's only automated
  checks).
- When the app is running, the MCP tools check behavior without clicking: `create_nodes` a few
  rectangles, then `align_nodes`/`distribute_nodes`, `update_nodes { rotation }` and `view_design` to look
  at the result; `get_nodes` to confirm the numbers (e.g. equal gaps after distribute).
- Manual checks in the app (by the user): drag near another node shows the pink guides and snaps,
  Ctrl disables it; resize a multi-selection; nudge with arrows and Ctrl+Z undoes a burst in one step;
  rotate with Shift snapping to 15° and resize a rotated node from a corner; drag a guide out of the
  ruler, snap to it, save, reopen and find it on the same page.
- Optional (recommended): add Vitest for `canvas/snapping/` and `canvas/arrange/`, which are pure
functions and easy to test.
</file>

import type {
  BlendMode,
  BoxSides,
  CanvasEffect,
  CanvasElement,
  ElementDefaults,

  StrokeAlign,
} from "@canvas";
import type { Graphics } from "pixi.js";
⋮----
import type { NodeSizing, SizeLimits } from "./node-layout.types";
import type { Paint } from "./paint.types";
⋮----
/**
 * What every element of a design is: a layer with a name, a place in the layer tree, visibility,
 * opacity, fills and strokes. Coordinates stay in world units (not relative to the parent), so
 * moving a frame moves its descendants with it (`withMembers`) and everything else needs no
 * transform. Element types extend it with their own fields.
 */
export interface DesignNode extends CanvasElement {
  /** The layer's name in the layers panel (and above root frames). */
  name: string;
  /**
   * The frame (or other container) holding it, `null` at the top of the page. Siblings are
   * ordered by `index`; a parent draws before its children.
   */
  parentId: string | null;
  /**
   * The page it's on (see the pages module). A node added without one (`""`) goes on the page on
   * screen; a node and everything it holds are always on the same page.
   */
  pageId: string;
  /** Hidden layers aren't drawn or hit, but stay in the layers panel. */
  visible: boolean;
  /** 0–1. On a frame or group it covers what it holds too, drawn together first. */
  opacity: number;
  /** How it blends with what's under it (see `LayerBlendMode`). */
  blendMode: LayerBlendMode;
  /** Painted bottom to top. */
  fills: Paint[];
  strokes: Paint[];
  /**
   * Stroke width in world units (with `strokeWeights`, the widest side's, so "has a stroke" checks
   * still read it).
   */
  strokeWeight: number;
  /** Where its strokes sit on a closed outline (open paths are always centered). */
  strokeAlign: StrokeAlign;
  /** How open ends and dashes end. */
  strokeCap: StrokeCap;
  /** How corners are joined. */
  strokeJoin: StrokeJoin;
  /** Corners sharper than this (degrees) are beveled instead of mitered, as in Figma. */
  strokeMiterAngle: number;
  /** Dash, gap, dash, gap… lengths in world units; empty for a solid stroke. */
  strokeDashes: number[];
  /**
   * Each side's own weight (Figma's individual strokes), on kinds with `sidedStrokes`; `null`
   * when every side has `strokeWeight`.
   */
  strokeWeights: BoxSides | null;
  /**
   * Whether it's a mask: it isn't drawn, and the siblings above it (up to the next mask) show
   * only through it, as in Figma.
   */
  isMask: boolean;
  /** How it masks (see `MaskType`). */
  maskType: MaskType;
  /** Whether what it masks shows only outside it (a cut-out) instead of inside it. */
  maskInverted: boolean;
  /**
   * Its effects, bottom to top (shadows, blurs, noise, glass, shaders; see the effects module):
   * drawn over it and what it holds, together.
   */
  effects: NodeEffect[];
  /**
   * How its width and height are decided in an auto layout (see `NodeSizing`). A text's hugging
   * follows its `autoResize`, so it stores only `fill` or `fixed`.
   */
  sizing: NodeSizing;
  /** Whether its auto layout parent leaves it where it is (Figma's "Ignore auto layout"). */
  layoutAbsolute: boolean;
  /** How small and large an auto layout may make it, or `null` without limits. */
  sizeLimits: SizeLimits | null;
}

   * Each side's own weight (Figma's individual strokes), on kinds with `sidedStrokes`; `null`

   */

   * Whether it's a mask: it isn't drawn, and the siblings above it (up to the next mask) show

   */

⋮----
/** Whether what it masks shows only outside it (a cut-out) instead of inside it. */

/**

/**
 * One effect of a node: a `CanvasEffect` (its `type` names the renderer that draws it) with the
 * type's own fields. The effects module defines the built-in types; plugins add their own.
 */
export type NodeEffect = CanvasEffect & Record<string, unknown>;
⋮----
/**
 * A layer's blend mode, Figma's: one of the canvas's `BlendMode`s, or `pass-through` (the
 * default), where a frame's or group's layers blend with what's behind it as if it weren't
 * there. On a layer that holds nothing, pass-through is normal.
 */
export type LayerBlendMode = "pass-through" | BlendMode;
⋮----
/**
 * How a mask shapes what it masks: by its opacity (`alpha`), by its outline alone (`vector`) or
 * by its brightness (`luminance`).

export type MaskType = MaskMode;
⋮----
/** Values every design node starts with (`NODE_DEFAULTS`). */
export interface NodeDefaults extends ElementDefaults {

  strokeCap: StrokeCap;
  strokeJoin: StrokeJoin;
  /** Figma's default miter angle (a miter limit of 4). */

  /** How a layer made a mask masks. */
  maskType: MaskType;
}

/** How a stroke's open ends and dashes end (Figma's names: `none` is a flat end at the point). */
export type StrokeCap = "none" | "round" | "square";
⋮----
/** How a stroke turns corners. */
export type StrokeJoin = "miter" | "bevel" | "round";
⋮----
/** How Pixi strokes a path (`drawPaints`): its ends, corners and miter limit (a ratio). */
export interface StrokeShape {

/**

  maskType?: string;
  /** Older files' vector masks, before `maskType`. */
  maskIsOutline?: boolean;
  /** A boolean's operation: `"UNION"`, `"INTERSECT"`, `"SUBTRACT"` or `"XOR"`. */
  booleanOperation?: string;
  resizeToFit?: boolean;
  count?: number;
  starInnerScale?: number;
  vectorData?: { vectorNetworkBlob?: number; normalizedSize?: FigVector };
  textData?: FigTextData;
  fontSize?: number;
  fontName?: { family?: string; style?: string };
  lineHeight?: FigNumber;
  letterSpacing?: FigNumber;
  textAlignHorizontal?: string;
  textAlignVertical?: string;
  textAutoResize?: string;
  textCase?: string;
  textDecoration?: string;
  paragraphSpacing?: number;
  autoRename?: boolean;
  symbolData?: FigSymbolData;
  derivedSymbolData?: FigOverride[];
  overriddenSymbolID?: FigGuid;
  componentPropRefs?: FigPropRef[];
  componentPropAssignments?: FigPropAssignment[];
  /** A page's ruler guides: `axis` `X` is a vertical line at x = `offset`. */
  guides?: { axis?: string; offset?: number }[];
  // FigJam
  /** A sticky's, shape's or connector's generated parts (its body, its text) and their looks. */
  nodeGenerationData?: { overrides?: FigOverride[] };
  derivedTextData?: FigTextLayout;
  /** A FigJam shape's outline: `SQUARE`, `ELLIPSE`, `DIAMOND`, `TRIANGLE_UP`, … */
  shapeWithTextType?: string;
  connectorStart?: FigConnectorEnd;
  connectorEnd?: FigConnectorEnd;
  /** `STRAIGHT`, `ELBOWED` or `CURVED`. */
  connectorLineStyle?: string;
  /** `NONE`, `ROUND`, `ARROW_LINES`, `ARROW_EQUILATERAL`, `TRIANGLE_FILLED`, … */
  connectorStartCap?: string;
  connectorEndCap?: string;
  /** A link preview widget's link (its fields are URL-encoded). */
  linkPreviewData?: { url?: string; title?: string };
  widgetMetadata?: { pluginID?: string; widgetName?: string };
}
⋮----
/** A style's or component's library key. */
⋮----
/** Set on style nodes: `TEXT`, `FILL`, `EFFECT` or `GRID`. */
⋮----
/** The text style it uses, whose typography wins over its own fields. */
⋮----
/** The color style of its fills, whose paints win over its own. */
⋮----
/** The color style of its strokes. */
⋮----
/** The effect style it uses, whose effects win over its own. */
⋮----
/** How the layer blends with what's under it: `PASS_THROUGH` (groups), `NORMAL`, `MULTIPLY`… */
⋮----
/** Auto layout: `HORIZONTAL` or `VERTICAL` (`NONE` or missing without one). */
⋮----
/** `INSIDE`, `CENTER` or `OUTSIDE`. */
⋮----
/** The longest miter, in stroke widths, before a corner is beveled. */
⋮----
/** Dash, gap… lengths; empty or missing for a solid stroke. */
⋮----
/** Whether each side of a box has its own stroke weight (`border*Weight`). */
⋮----
/** Whether the layer is a mask of the siblings above it. */
⋮----
/** How it masks: `"ALPHA"`, `"OUTLINE"` (Figma's vector mask) or `"LUMINANCE"`. */
⋮----
/** Older files' vector masks, before `maskType`. */
⋮----
/** A boolean's operation: `"UNION"`, `"INTERSECT"`, `"SUBTRACT"` or `"XOR"`. */
⋮----
/** A page's ruler guides: `axis` `X` is a vertical line at x = `offset`. */
⋮----
// FigJam
/** A sticky's, shape's or connector's generated parts (its body, its text) and their looks. */
⋮----
/** A FigJam shape's outline: `SQUARE`, `ELLIPSE`, `DIAMOND`, `TRIANGLE_UP`, … */
⋮----
/** `STRAIGHT`, `ELBOWED` or `CURVED`. */
⋮----
/** `NONE`, `ROUND`, `ARROW_LINES`, `ARROW_EQUILATERAL`, `TRIANGLE_FILLED`, … */
⋮----
/** A link preview widget's link (its fields are URL-encoded). */
⋮----
/** A node with its children, instances expanded into their component's (overridden) nodes. */
export interface ResolvedFigNode {
  node: FigNode;
  children: ResolvedFigNode[];

<file path="src-tauri/Cargo.toml">
[package]
name = "cloudy-canvas"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Cloudy Canvas — boards and designs on one canvas"
authors = ["DarkRedgm"]
license = "AGPL-3.0-only"
repository = "https://github.com/Cloudy-Studio-Apps/cloudy-canvas"
edition = "2024"

# See more keys and their definitions at https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html

[lib]

# The `_lib` suffix may seem redundant but it is necessary

# to make the lib name unique and wouldn't conflict with the bin name.

# This seems to be only an issue on Windows, see https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/8519

name = "cloudy_canvas_lib"
crate-type = ["staticlib", "cdylib", "rlib"]

[build-dependencies]
tauri-build = { version = "2", features = [] }

[dependencies]
tauri = { version = "2", features = [] }
tauri-plugin-dialog = "2"
tauri-plugin-fs = "2"
tauri-plugin-clipboard-manager = "2"
tauri-plugin-opener = "2"
tauri-plugin-http = "2"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
axum = { version = "0.8", default-features = false, features = ["http1", "tokio"] }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["net", "sync", "time"] }
tauri-plugin-deep-link = "2"
fontdb = "0.23"

[target.'cfg(any(target_os = "macos", windows, target_os = "linux"))'.dependencies]
tauri-plugin-process = "2"
tauri-plugin-single-instance = { version = "2", features = ["deep-link"] }
tauri-plugin-updater = "2"

# Read the optimization guideline for more details: https://tauri.app/concept/size/#cargo-configuration

[profile.release]
codegen-units = 1
lto = true
opt-level = 3
panic = "abort"
strip = true
</file>

<file path="src/app/plugins/plugin-api.types.ts">
import type { createId, defineModule, definePoint, PluginManifest } from "@shared/core";
import type { notifyError, toast } from "@shared/stores/toast-store";
import type { boardLibrary } from "@board/ui/components/library";
import type { boardEditor } from "@board/ui";
⋮----
import type { designEditor } from "@design/ui";
⋮----
import type { useDesignEngine, useDesignState } from "@design/ui/design-engine-context";
⋮----
/**
 * What a plugin's `activate(api)` gets: the app's own building blocks, so a plugin needs no
 * imports (and shares the app's React). Version 1 (`PLUGIN_API_VERSION`).
 */
export interface PluginApi {
  apiVersion: number;
  plugin: {
    id: string;
    manifest: PluginManifest;
    /** A file in the plugin's folder (e.g. an icon), relative to it. */
    readAsset(path: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;
    /** Reads a text file in the plugin's folder (e.g. an SVG icon). */
    readText(path: string): Promise<string>;
  };
  core: {
    defineModule: typeof defineModule;
    definePoint: typeof definePoint;
    createId: typeof createId;
  };
  canvas: Pick<
    typeof canvas,
    | "ElementKind"
    | "BoxKind"
    | "TextBoxKind"
    | "LineKind"
    | "ELEMENT_DEFAULTS"
    | "createElementBase"
    | "defineService"
    | "selectAndEdit"
    | "asUndoStep"
    | "buildElement"
    | "summarizeElement"
    | "stringArg"
    | "optionalString"
    | "optionalNumber"
    | "optionalBoolean"
    | "optionalChoice"
    | "stringList"
    | "optionalRecord"
    | "recordList"
    | "clamp"
    | "roundPoint"
    | "fitInView"
    | "elementBounds"
    | "rotatePoint"
    | "scaleRect"
    | "scaleLength"
    | "toUnrotated"
    | "gradientCss"
    | "gradientHandles"
    | "transformFromHandles"
    | "pastThreshold"
    | "DRAW_THRESHOLD_PX"
    | "MOVE_THRESHOLD_PX"
    | "FreehandTool"
    | "smoothPoints"
    | "measureTextBlock"
    | "textFont"
    | "fontFamilyList"
  >;
  ui: {
    React: typeof React;
    toast: typeof toast;
    notifyError: typeof notifyError;
  } & Pick<
    typeof canvasUi,
    | "FloatingPanel"
    | "PanelDivider"
    | "ToolButton"
    | "OptionButton"
    | "ColorSwatch"
    | "ColorPalette"
    | "ExtensionIconView"
    | "useEngine"
    | "useEngineState"
    | "useService"
    | "useEngineElement"
  >;
  board: {
    /** The board's canvas points (kinds, tools, options, hooks, …). */
    canvas: typeof board.boardCanvas;
    /** The board editor's points (tools, panels, top bar, overlays, …). */
    editor: typeof boardEditor;
    agentTools: typeof board.boardAgentTools;
    library: typeof boardLibrary;
    requireBoard: typeof board.requireBoard;
    palette: Pick<
      typeof board,
      "STICKY_COLORS" | "SHAPE_FILLS" | "SHAPE_STROKES" | "LINE_COLORS" | "INK_COLOR"
    >;
  };
  design: DesignPluginApi;
}
⋮----
/** A file in the plugin's folder (e.g. an icon), relative to it. */
readAsset(path: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;
/** Reads a text file in the plugin's folder (e.g. an SVG icon). */
readText(path: string): Promise<string>;
⋮----
/** The board's canvas points (kinds, tools, options, hooks, …). */
⋮----
/** The board editor's points (tools, panels, top bar, overlays, …). */
⋮----
/** What design plugins build on (`api.design`). */
export interface DesignPluginApi {
  /** The design's canvas points (kinds, tools, options, view, hooks, …). */
  canvas: typeof design.designCanvas;
  /**
   * The design editor's points: the shared ones (tools, toolPanels, overlays, …) plus
   * `leftTabs`, `propertySections` and `mainMenu`.
   */
  editor: typeof designEditor;
  migrations: typeof design.designMigrations;
  /** Agent tools on the open design, one group per module (`requireDesign` gets the design). */
  agentTools: typeof design.designAgentTools;
  requireDesign: typeof design.requireDesign;
  /** The layer tree service (`useService(DESIGN_TREE)`). */
  tree: typeof design.DESIGN_TREE;
  /** The pages service (`useService(DESIGN_PAGES)`); the page on screen is `engine.scope`. */
  pages: typeof design.DESIGN_PAGES;
  /** The node base every design element extends, and its helpers. */
  nodes: Pick<
    typeof design,
    | "DesignNodeKind"
    | "createNodeBase"
    | "isDesignNode"
    | "solidPaint"
    | "imagePaint"
    | "gradientPaint"
    | "isGradientPaint"
    | "drawPaints"
    | "traceBox"
    | "NODE_DEFAULTS"
    | "BoxShapeKind"
    | "PointsShapeKind"
    | "NodeDrawTool"
    | "BoxDrawTool"
    | "containerAt"
    | "parentFor"
    | "layerNameOf"
    | "pointsInBox"
    | "pointInPolygon"
    | "distanceToOutline"
  >;
  /**
   * Vector networks (vertices, bezier segments, filled regions): building them (from shapes too),
   * placing, hit testing, tracing, editing, and the edit mode's base tool and session.
   */
  network: Pick<
    typeof design,
    | "polylineNetwork"
    | "polygonNetwork"
    | "rectNetwork"
    | "ellipseNetwork"
    | "placeNetwork"
    | "scaleNetwork"
    | "networkBounds"
    | "hitSegment"
    | "vertexAt"
    | "insideRegion"
    | "traceStrokes"
    | "traceRegions"
    | "splitSegment"
    | "connect"
    | "addVertex"
    | "moveVertices"
    | "setTangent"
    | "removeParts"
    | "cutSegment"
    | "bendSegment"
    | "toggleSmooth"
    | "toggleRegion"
    | "networkFaces"
    | "faceAt"
    | "VectorEditTool"
    | "VECTOR_EDIT"
    | "VECTOR_TOOLS"
  >;
  /** Building blocks of the side panels, for tabs and property sections. */
  panel: Pick<
    typeof designPanel,
    | "PanelSection"
    | "PanelIconButton"
    | "PanelAddButton"
    | "NumberField"
    | "NodeNumberField"
    | "NodeSelectField"
    | "NodeCheckbox"
    | "NodeOptionButtons"
    | "FieldBox"
    | "HexInput"
    | "PercentInput"
    | "PaintField"
    | "PropertyGrid"
    | "sharedValue"
  >;
  /** Filters for `propertySections` entries' `when`. */
  sections: Pick<typeof designModules, "ofType" | "allKinds" | "someNodes" | "noNodes">;
  /**
   * Effects of a plugin's own: a renderer on `canvas.effectRenderers` (drawn on the GPU with
   * these shaders and helpers), an entry on `editor.effectTypes` (`defineEffectType`, with these
   * fields) and how agents give it (`setEffectReader`).
   */
  effects: Pick<typeof designModules, "defineEffectType"> &
    Pick<
      typeof design,
      "setEffectReader" | "localUniforms" | "LOCAL_GLSL" | "LOCAL_UNIFORMS" | "NOISE_GLSL"
    > &
    Pick<
      typeof canvasApi,
      | "EffectShader"
      | "FILTER_HEADER"
      | "SAMPLING_GLSL"
      | "silhouetteShader"
      | "underShader"
      | "atopShader"
      | "shapeUnderShader"
    > &
    typeof effectFields;
  hooks: Pick<typeof designHooks, "useSelectedNodes" | "useEditNodes" | "useMoveNodes"> & {
    useDesignEngine: typeof useDesignEngine;
    useDesignState: typeof useDesignState;
  };
}
⋮----

⋮----

   * The design editor's points: the shared ones (tools, toolPanels, overlays, …) plus
   * `leftTabs`, `propertySections` and `mainMenu`.
   */
⋮----
/** Agent tools on the open design, one group per module (`requireDesign` gets the design). */

/** The layer tree service (`useService(DESIGN_TREE)`). */
⋮----
/** The pages service (`useService(DESIGN_PAGES)`); the page on screen is `engine.scope`. */
⋮----
/** The node base every design element extends, and its helpers. */
⋮----
/**
   * Vector networks (vertices, bezier segments, filled regions): building them (from shapes too),
   * placing, hit testing, tracing, editing, and the edit mode's base tool and session.
   */
⋮----
/** Building blocks of the side panels, for tabs and property sections. */
⋮----
/** Filters for `propertySections` entries' `when`. */
⋮----
/**
   * Effects of a plugin's own: a renderer on `canvas.effectRenderers` (drawn on the GPU with

import { rectContainsPoint } from "../geometry";

import type { ElementView } from "../render/element-view";
import { ELEMENT_DEFAULTS } from "./element.defaults";
import { scaleRect } from "./element-scale";
import type { ScaleTransform } from "./element-scale.types";
import type { CanvasElement, ElementPatch, ElementStyle } from "./element.types";
import type { ElementInteraction, InteractionQuery } from "./element.interaction.types";
import type {
  ElementBuildContext,

⋮----
/**
 * Behavior of one element type. Elements are plain data; each product registers one kind instance
 * per type in its `ElementKinds`, and the engine asks it how to draw, hit-test, move, resize, edit
 * and restyle the elements of that type. Subclasses override the defaults below. `O` is the
 * product's tool options, which `optionsOf` and `restyle` read and write.
 */
export abstract class ElementKind<
E extends CanvasElement = CanvasElement,
⋮----
/** The stored `type` of the elements this kind handles. */
⋮----
/** Human name, e.g. "Sticky note". Also names the text editor ("Sticky note text"). */
⋮----
/** One sentence for tooltips and listings. */

⋮----

⋮----

⋮----

   * selection only follow it (see `scale`).

⋮----
/**

   * further back, and a marquee selects them only when it encloses them.
   */
⋮----
/** Whether connectors (and other lines that attach to elements) can attach to it. */
⋮----
/** Whether selection and hover outline its bounds (lines show their handles instead). */
⋮----
/**

   * rotate commands. The engine draws, hits and outlines it turned; the kind works unturned.
   */
⋮----
/** JSON schema of the type-specific spec fields agents may give (read from `spec.args`). */
⋮----
/** Fields agents may patch; `null` allows every field. */
⋮----
/**

   * properties carry (`styleOf`, `applyStyle`). Fields match by name across types.

⋮----

bounds(el: E): Rect

import type { CanvasProduct, CanvasScopes, SelectTargetRequest } from "../canvas-product.types";

⋮----
/** A tool a module adds, with its shortcuts (bound to `tool.<id>`). */
export interface ProductTool<O extends object> {
  id: string;
  create(ctx: ToolContext<O>): Tool;
  keys?: readonly Shortcut[];
}
⋮----
create(ctx: ToolContext<O>): Tool;
⋮----
/** A command the editor implements (see `CanvasProduct.hostCommands`). */
export interface HostCommand {
  id: string;
  /** Its name in shortcut lists and tooltips. */
  label: string;
  keys?: readonly Shortcut[];
}
⋮----
/** Its name in shortcut lists and tooltips. */
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.resolveElements`; hooks run one after another in module order. */
export type ResolveElementsHook<O extends object> = (
  elements: CanvasElement[],
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => CanvasElement[];
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.withMembers`; each hook adds to what the earlier ones returned. */
export type WithMembersHook<O extends object> = (
  ids: ReadonlySet<string>,
  elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  purpose: "move" | "delete",
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => Set<string>;
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.orderKeys`; only one module may give the drawing order. */
export type DrawOrderHook<O extends object> = (
  elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => Map<string, string>;
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.clips`; only one module may give the clips. */
export type ClipsHook<O extends object> = (
  elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => Map<string, ElementClip>;
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.masks`; only one module may give the masks. */
export type MasksHook<O extends object> = (
  elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => ElementMasks;
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.effects`; only one module may give the effects. */
export type EffectsHook<O extends object> = (
  elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => ElementEffects;
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.undrawn`; only one module may give it. */
export type UndrawnHook<O extends object> = (
  elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => ReadonlySet<string>;
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.selectTarget`; only one module may decide it. */
export type SelectTargetHook<O extends object> = (
  hitId: string,
  request: SelectTargetRequest,
  elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => string;
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.alignTarget`; only one module may decide it. */
export type AlignTargetHook<O extends object> = (
  el: CanvasElement,
  elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => Rect | null;
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.rulerFrame`; only one module may decide it. */
export type RulerFrameHook<O extends object> = (
  selected: readonly CanvasElement[],
  elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => CanvasElement | null;
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.frames`; only one module may give them. */
export type FramesHook<O extends object> = (
  elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => readonly CanvasElement[];
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.editElement`; only one module may give it. */
export type EditElementHook<O extends object> = (el: CanvasElement, ctx: ToolContext<O>) => boolean;
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.afterEdit`; only one module may give it. */
export type AfterEditHook<O extends object> = (
  doc: CanvasDocument,
  change: EditedChange,
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => void;
⋮----
/** See `CanvasProduct.onMoved`; hooks run one after another in module order. */
export type OnMovedHook<O extends object> = (
  doc: CanvasDocument,
  moved: ReadonlySet<string>,
  elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => void;
export type OnRemoveHook = NonNullable<CanvasProduct["onRemove"]>;
export type PrepareCopiesHook = NonNullable<CanvasProduct["prepareCopies"]>;
/** See `CanvasProduct.pasteText`; the first hook that returns an element wins. */
export type PasteTextHook<O extends object> = NonNullable<CanvasProduct<O>["pasteText"]>;
/** See `CanvasProduct.pasteOnto`; the first hook that returns patches wins. */
export type PasteOntoHook<O extends object> = (
  text: string,
  selected: readonly CanvasElement[],
  kinds: ElementKinds<O>,
) => Map<string, ElementPatch> | null;
/** See `CanvasProduct.pasteImage`; the first hook that returns an element wins. */
export type PasteImageHook<O extends object> = NonNullable<CanvasProduct<O>["pasteImage"]>;
⋮----
/**
 * The points a product's canvas is assembled from (`composeProduct`). Each product has its own
 * set (`createCanvasPoints`), typed with its tool options `O`.
 */
export interface CanvasPoints<O extends object> {
  kinds: ExtensionPoint<ElementKind<CanvasElement, O>>;
  tools: ExtensionPoint<ProductTool<O>>;
  hostCommands: ExtensionPoint<HostCommand>;
  /** Shortcuts of other commands. A command bound twice throws. */
  keybindings: ExtensionPoint<Keybindings>;
  /** Default values of the tool options a module owns. An option given twice throws. */
  options: ExtensionPoint<Partial<O>>;
  /** The canvas's zoom range and grid. A value given twice throws. */
  view: ExtensionPoint<Partial<CanvasViewOptions>>;
  /** The scopes the canvas is split into (one module at most; two throw). */
  scopes: ExtensionPoint<CanvasScopes>;
  /** Where the ruler guides are kept (one module at most; two throw). */
  guides: ExtensionPoint<CanvasGuides>;
  /** The drawing order (one module at most; two throw). */
  drawOrder: ExtensionPoint<DrawOrderHook<O>>;
  /** What clips each element (one module at most; two throw). */
  clips: ExtensionPoint<ClipsHook<O>>;
  /** What masks each element (one module at most; two throw). */
  masks: ExtensionPoint<MasksHook<O>>;
  /** Each element's effects (one module at most; two throw). */
  effects: ExtensionPoint<EffectsHook<O>>;
  /** How each type of effect is drawn (keyed by type: two renderers of one type throw). */
  effectRenderers: ExtensionPoint<EffectRenderer>;
  /** What isn't drawn on its own (one module at most; two throw). */
  undrawn: ExtensionPoint<UndrawnHook<O>>;
  /** What a click selects (one module at most; two throw). */
  selectTarget: ExtensionPoint<SelectTargetHook<O>>;
  /** What a single element aligns with (one module at most; two throw). */
  alignTarget: ExtensionPoint<AlignTargetHook<O>>;
  /** What the rulers measure (one module at most; two throw). */
  rulerFrame: ExtensionPoint<RulerFrameHook<O>>;
  /** The frames N and Shift+N step through (one module at most; two throw). */
  frames: ExtensionPoint<FramesHook<O>>;
  /** What double-click or Enter edits (one module at most; two throw). */
  editElement: ExtensionPoint<EditElementHook<O>>;
  onMoved: ExtensionPoint<OnMovedHook<O>>;
  /** What follows from every edit (one module at most; two throw). */
  afterEdit: ExtensionPoint<AfterEditHook<O>>;
  links: ExtensionPoint<() => CanvasLinks>;
  resolveElements: ExtensionPoint<ResolveElementsHook<O>>;
  withMembers: ExtensionPoint<WithMembersHook<O>>;
  onRemove: ExtensionPoint<OnRemoveHook>;
  prepareCopies: ExtensionPoint<PrepareCopiesHook>;
  pasteText: ExtensionPoint<PasteTextHook<O>>;
  pasteOnto: ExtensionPoint<PasteOntoHook<O>>;
  pasteImage: ExtensionPoint<PasteImageHook<O>>;
}

import type { Camera } from "../camera";
import type { CanvasDocument } from "../document";
import type { CanvasElement, ElementKinds } from "../elements";
import type { Interaction, ResizeMode } from "../handles";
import type { Guide } from "../links";
import type { Point, Rect } from "../geometry.types";
import type { RulerGuide } from "../ruler-guides";
import type { ServiceDef } from "../services";
import type { SnapAxis, SnapFeedback, Snapper } from "../snapping";
⋮----
export interface CanvasPointer {
  screen: Point;
  world: Point;
  shiftKey: boolean;
  /** Ctrl on Windows/Linux, Cmd on macOS. */
  modKey: boolean;
  altKey: boolean;
}
⋮----
/** Ctrl on Windows/Linux, Cmd on macOS. */
⋮----
/** What tools can do to the engine. `O` is the product's tool options. */
export interface ToolContext<O extends object = object> {
  readonly doc: CanvasDocument;
  readonly camera: Camera;
  readonly kinds: ElementKinds<O>;
  /** A service of the engine (e.g. a board's ER diagrams), created on first use. */
  service<T>(def: ServiceDef<T>): T;
  getOptions(): O;
  getSelection(): ReadonlySet<string>;
  setSelection(ids: Iterable<string>): void;
  setTool(tool: string): void;
  /** The active tool's id. */
  getTool(): string;
  elementAt(world: Point): CanvasElement | undefined;
  /**
   * What a click at `world` selects (the product's `selectTarget`, e.g. the group around what's
   * hit); `deep` (Ctrl/Cmd) selects what's hit itself.
   */
  targetAt(world: Point, deep: boolean): CanvasElement | undefined;
  /** What selecting this element selects instead (e.g. its group), as `targetAt` does. */
  targetOf(id: string): string;
  /** An element as the scene sees it. */
  getElement(id: string): CanvasElement | undefined;
  elementsInRect(rect: Rect): CanvasElement[];
  /** The ids plus what moves with them (e.g. an entity's attributes). */
  withMembers(ids: Iterable<string>): Set<string>;
  /**
   * Tells the product elements were just dragged to a new place (`CanvasProduct.onMoved`, e.g.
   * dropped into a frame), in the current undo step.
   */
  moved(ids: Iterable<string>): void;
  /**
   * Adds copies of the elements (with what moves with them) in place, as a new undo step.
   * Returns original id → copy id.
   */
  duplicate(ids: Iterable<string>): Map<string, string>;
  /** Edits an element's text, or one text part of it (e.g. a table cell). */
  editText(id: string, part?: string): void;
  /** Types the text of a new element; it's added to the document (and selected) on commit. */
  editNewText(el: CanvasElement): void;
  /**
   * Selects a part of the single selected element (e.g. a table row), which the overlay outlines
   * and Delete removes; `null` clears it.
   */
  setPart(part: string | null): void;
  getPart(): string | null;
  setCursor(cursor: string): void;
  setHover(id: string | null): void;
  getHover(): string | null;
  setMarquee(rect: Rect | null): void;
  /**
   * Shows an element that isn't in the document yet (e.g. the stroke being drawn), drawn by its
   * kind like any other element. `null` clears it.
   */
  setDraft(el: CanvasElement | null): void;
  /** Dims elements, e.g. those a gesture will remove when it ends; `null` clears it. */
  setFaded(ids: Iterable<string> | null): void;
  /** Shows gesture feedback above the elements (e.g. a line being dragged); `null` clears it. */
  setGuide(guide: Guide | null): void;
  /**
   * Snapping for one gesture: to the elements on screen but these ids (what's being moved, with
   * its members), following the user's snap settings. Clear it when the gesture ends.
   */
  createSnapper(exclude: Iterable<string>): Snapper;
  /** Shows smart guides or measurements (e.g. Alt + hover distances); `null` clears them. */
  setSnapFeedback(feedback: SnapFeedback | null): void;
  /** Plays a quick pop on elements just added to the document (e.g. a stamped sticker). */
  animateIn(ids: readonly string[]): void;
  /** The ruler guides of the scope on screen (see `CanvasGuides`); empty when there are none. */
  guides(): readonly RulerGuide[];
  /**
   * Replaces the scope's ruler guides, in the current undo step (`doc.checkpoint()` first for a new
   * one). Ignored when the product keeps none.
   */
  setGuides(guides: readonly RulerGuide[]): void;
  /** Shows the value of the guide at this index while it's dragged; `null` hides it. */
  setActiveGuide(index: number | null): void;
  /** Whether a screen point is over the shown ruler guides of `axis` come out of (see `overRuler`). */
  overRuler(axis: SnapAxis, screen: Point): boolean;
  /** Handle under the point (e.g. a resize handle), if any. */
  interactionAt(world: Point): Interaction | null;
  /** Pans while `screen` is near the viewport edge; `null` stops. `onPan` runs after each step. */
  autoPan(screen: Point | null, onPan?: () => void): void;
  panBy(dx: number, dy: number): void;
  /** Hands an element's action (e.g. "play") to the host, which decides what it does. */
  activate(elementId: string, action: string): void;
  requestRender(): void;
}
⋮----
/** A service of the engine (e.g. a board's ER diagrams), created on first use. */
service<T>(def: ServiceDef<T>): T;
getOptions(): O;
getSelection(): ReadonlySet<string>;
setSelection(ids: Iterable<string>): void;
setTool(tool: string): void;
/** The active tool's id. */
getTool(): string;
elementAt(world: Point): CanvasElement | undefined;
/**
   * What a click at `world` selects (the product's `selectTarget`, e.g. the group around what's
   * hit); `deep` (Ctrl/Cmd) selects what's hit itself.
   */
targetAt(world: Point, deep: boolean): CanvasElement | undefined;
/** What selecting this element selects instead (e.g. its group), as `targetAt` does. */
targetOf(id: string): string;
/** An element as the scene sees it. */
getElement(id: string): CanvasElement | undefined;
elementsInRect(rect: Rect): CanvasElement[];
/** The ids plus what moves with them (e.g. an entity's attributes). */
withMembers(ids: Iterable<string>): Set<string>;
/**
   * Tells the product elements were just dragged to a new place (`CanvasProduct.onMoved`, e.g.

   */
moved(ids: Iterable<string>): void;
/**

   * Returns original id → copy id.
   */
duplicate(ids: Iterable<string>): Map<string, string>;
/** Edits an element's text, or one text part of it (e.g. a table cell). */
editText(id: string, part?: string): void;
/** Types the text of a new element; it's added to the document (and selected) on commit. */
editNewText(el: CanvasElement): void;
/**
   * Selects a part of the single selected element (e.g. a table row), which the overlay outlines
   * and Delete removes; `null` clears it.
   */
setPart(part: string | null): void;
getPart(): string | null;
setCursor(cursor: string): void;
setHover(id: string | null): void;
getHover(): string | null;
setMarquee(rect: Rect | null): void;
/**
   * Shows an element that isn't in the document yet (e.g. the stroke being drawn), drawn by its
   * kind like any other element. `null` clears it.
   */
setDraft(el: CanvasElement | null): void;
/** Dims elements, e.g. those a gesture will remove when it ends; `null` clears it. */
setFaded(ids: Iterable<string> | null): void;
/** Shows gesture feedback above the elements (e.g. a line being dragged); `null` clears it. */
setGuide(guide: Guide | null): void;
/**
   * Snapping for one gesture: to the elements on screen but these ids (what's being moved, with
   * its members), following the user's snap settings. Clear it when the gesture ends.
   */
createSnapper(exclude: Iterable<string>): Snapper;
/** Shows smart guides or measurements (e.g. Alt + hover distances); `null` clears them. */
setSnapFeedback(feedback: SnapFeedback | null): void;
/** Plays a quick pop on elements just added to the document (e.g. a stamped sticker). */
animateIn(ids: readonly string[]): void;
/** The ruler guides of the scope on screen (see `CanvasGuides`); empty when there are none. */
guides(): readonly RulerGuide[];
/**
   * Replaces the scope's ruler guides, in the current undo step (`doc.checkpoint()` first for a new
   * one). Ignored when the product keeps none.

setGuides(guides: readonly RulerGuide[]): void;
/** Shows the value of the guide at this index while it's dragged; `null` hides it. */
setActiveGuide(index: number | null): void;
/** Whether a screen point is over the shown ruler guides of `axis` come out of (see `overRuler`). */
overRuler(axis: SnapAxis, screen: Point): boolean;
/** Handle under the point (e.g. a resize handle), if any. */
interactionAt(world: Point): Interaction | null;
/** Pans while `screen` is near the viewport edge; `null` stops. `onPan` runs after each step. */
autoPan(screen: Point | null, onPan?: ()
panBy(dx: number, dy: number): void;
/** Hands an element's action (e.g. "play") to the host, which decides what it does. */
activate(elementId: string, action: string): void;
requestRender(): void;
⋮----
/** A tool. Products add theirs next to the built-in select and hand tools. */
export interface Tool {
  /** Unique per product; its keymap command is `tool.<id>`. */
  readonly id: string;
  readonly cursor: string;
  /**
   * What the selection's resize handles do while it's on (and whether a selection that only
   * scales gets them): the Scale tool's `scale`. Unset is `resize`.
   */
  readonly resizeMode?: ResizeMode;
  onPointerDown(p: CanvasPointer): void;
  onPointerMove?(p: CanvasPointer): void;
  onPointerUp?(p: CanvasPointer): void;
  /** Pointer moved without a button pressed. */
  onHover?(p: CanvasPointer): void;
  /** The camera moved (wheel, zoom controls, auto-pan) — e.g. mid-gesture. */
  onCameraChange?(): void;
  /** Tool switched away or the gesture was cancelled. */
  onCancel?(): void;
  /** The tool was just switched to (e.g. to show feedback that stays while it's on). */
  onActivate?(): void;
  /**
   * A command (`deleteSelection`, `cancel`, …) while the tool is on: returns `true` when the tool
   * handled it, so the engine's own handler doesn't run (e.g. an edit mode's Delete).
   */
  onCommand?(command: string): boolean;
}
⋮----

⋮----

<file path="src/products/design/modules/core/node/design-node.kind.ts">
import {
  BoxKind,
  type ElementBuildContext,
  type ElementClip,
  type ElementDescription,
  type ElementPatch,
  type ElementSpec,
  type ElementStyle,
  type ElementView,
  type Point,
  type Rect,
  rotatePoint,
  scaleLength,
  type ScaleTransform,
  type BoxSides,
  dashPath,
  distanceToPath,
  type PathShape,
  pointInPath,
  strokeArea,
} from "@canvas";
⋮----
import type { DesignToolOptions } from "../../../design-options.types";
import { applyNodeSpec } from "./apply-node-spec";
import { checkNodePatch } from "./check-node-patch";
import type { DesignNode, NodeGeometry, NodeStroke } from "./design-node.types";
import {
  hasVisibleStroke,
  STROKE_CACHE,
  strokeAreaOptions,
  strokeKey,
  strokeReach,
  strokeShapeOf,
} from "./node-stroke";
import { GEOMETRY_CACHE } from "./node-geometry";
import type { NodeBuildContext } from "./node-build.types";
import { flipPaints } from "./flip-paints";
import { scaleTiles } from "./scale-tiles";
import { flipPlacement } from "./flip-placement";
import type { FlipAxis } from "./flip.types";
import { NODE_DEFAULTS } from "./node.defaults";
import { FIXED_SIZING } from "./node-layout";
import type { LayoutAxis } from "./node-layout.types";
import { NODE_STYLE_FIELDS, nodeStylePatch } from "./node-style";
⋮----
/**
 * The base of every design element type. It handles what all nodes share (name, place in the
 * tree, visibility, opacity, fills and strokes, the images they show); a subclass gives its
 * `type`, `label`, `description` and `draw` (with `drawPaints`). Plugins extend it the same way.
 */
export abstract class DesignNodeKind<E extends DesignNode = DesignNode> extends BoxKind<
⋮----
/** Layers turn (`rotation`, round their top-left corner); the engine draws and hits them turned. */
⋮----
/** Whether agents can create it (`create_nodes`); kinds that can give `nodeFromSpec`. */
⋮----
/**
   * Whether it holds other nodes (a frame). Nodes drawn or dropped inside a container go into the
   * topmost one under them; moving or deleting it takes its children along.
   */
⋮----
/**
   * The area its children show in, when it clips them (a frame with "Clip content"), in world
   * units; `null` lets them overflow.
   */
contentClip(_el: E): ElementClip | null
⋮----
/**
   * Whether it may go into this container when drawn or dropped there (sections only go into
   * sections; everything else into any container).
   */
canGoInto(_parent: DesignNode, _parentKind: DesignNodeKind): boolean
⋮----
/** Opacity, fills and strokes; kinds add their own (a corner radius, a font). */
⋮----
/** The pasted look as it can show it (no fills on a line, no strokes on a text). */
override applyStyle(el: E, style: ElementStyle): ElementPatch<E>
⋮----
/** Whether it has an inside to fill (lines don't: they only show strokes). */
⋮----
/** Whether it shows strokes (text doesn't yet). */
⋮----
/** Whether its fills can be images (text can't: its fill is its color). */
⋮----
/**
   * Its shape in local coordinates (see `NodeGeometry`): what it draws, is hit by, masks with as a
   * vector mask and takes part in booleans with. `null` when it has none (a text whose font isn't
   * loaded yet), so it masks by its pixels. Cached by `geometryKey`; kinds give `buildGeometry`.
   */
geometry(el: E): NodeGeometry | null
⋮----
/**
   * Whether it's made of its children (a group, a boolean; see `ChildHostKind`): a click on a
   * child selects it until it's entered.
   */
⋮----
/**
   * Whether what it holds is drawn on its own (a boolean's operands aren't: it draws their
   * result). What isn't drawn can still be clicked (selecting the boolean) and entered.
   */
⋮----
/**
   * Whether it has a shape of its own (a group's is its children's): masks and booleans made of
   * it take its geometry, else only its children's.
   */
⋮----
/**
   * What its geometry depends on, as a string (its size by default; kinds add their shape's
   * fields). Two nodes with the same key share one geometry.
   */
geometryKey(el: E): string
⋮----
/**
   * Whether each side of its box can have its own stroke weight (`strokeWeights`; rectangles and
   * frames). Kinds that say so give `sidedStrokeArea`.
   */
⋮----
/** The area its stroke covers with a weight per side; `null` when the kind has no sides. */
protected sidedStrokeArea(_el: E, _sides: BoxSides): PathShape | null
⋮----
/**
   * Whether its one-weight stroke is the same band `sidedStrokeArea` makes (a box's undashed
   * stroke whose corners its joins don't change), worked out exactly from the box instead of
   * outlined.
   */
protected boxStroke(_el: E): boolean
⋮----
/**
   * The area its stroke covers (local coordinates; aligned, dashed, sided): what Outline stroke
   * makes and what a boolean takes from an operand that fills nothing. Empty without a weight.
   * Cached by its shape and stroke keys.
   */
strokeArea(el: E): PathShape
⋮----
/**
   * How its visible strokes are drawn (`drawPaints`), or `null` when it shows none: centered
   * strokes (solid or dashed) and open paths are Pixi strokes along the path, which stay smooth
   * at any zoom and need no outlining; aligned and sided ones fill their `strokeArea`.
   */
strokeOf(el: E): NodeStroke | null
⋮----
/** Works out its geometry (`geometry` caches it); none by default. */
protected buildGeometry(_el: E): NodeGeometry | null
⋮----
/** Its name in the layers panel: the one it was given, or one it derives (e.g. a text's). */
layerName(el: E): string
⋮----
/**
   * Draws the node in local coordinates, usually with `drawPaints(view, el, outline)`, which also
   * applies its opacity and visibility.
   */
abstract override draw(view: ElementView, el: E): void;
⋮----
/** Visible nodes are hit by their shape (`hitsShape`) or by their stroke where it reaches out. */
override hitTest(el: E, p: Point, tolerance: number): boolean
⋮----
/** Whether `p` (world, unturned) is on its shape: anywhere in its bounds by default. */
protected hitsShape(el: E, p: Point, tolerance: number): boolean
⋮----
/** Whether `p` (world, unturned) is on its visible stroke (an outside stroke reaches past it). */
protected hitsStroke(el: E, p: Point, tolerance: number): boolean
⋮----
/**
   * Whether it looks the same upside down (rectangles, ellipses, frames). Ones that don't (a
   * polygon's point) turn half round when flipped top to bottom, which draws them mirrored.
   */
⋮----
/** Its angle as the panel shows it: its `rotation` (a line's runs along its ends). */
turnOf(el: E): number
⋮----
/**
   * Patch that mirrors it across the line `at` on `axis` (flip horizontal or vertical): the same
   * shape in the mirrored place, turned the other way.
   */
flip(el: E, axis: FlipAxis, at: number): ElementPatch<E>
⋮----
// Upside down: half a turn round its middle mirrors a shape symmetric left to right.
⋮----
// Turned half round, its box is mirrored left to right where the shape looks mirrored.
⋮----
/**
   * Scaled (the Scale tool): its geometry as the kind scales it, its stroke weight and its tiled
   * images' tiles.
   */
override scale(el: E, t: ScaleTransform): ElementPatch<E>
⋮----
/**
   * Resized by hand (or by an agent): the sides that change stop hugging or filling, as in Figma.
   * Kinds resize their shape in `resizeShape`; auto layout keeps the sizing it resizes with.
   */
override resize(el: E, rect: Rect): ElementPatch<E>
⋮----
/** Its patch for a new box (stretched by default). */
protected resizeShape(el: E, rect: Rect): ElementPatch<E>
⋮----
/**
   * Whether its size on `axis` is what it holds (an auto layout frame's hug, a text's auto size),
   * so an auto layout parent takes it as it is and only its own layout changes it.
   */
hugs(_el: E, _axis: LayoutAxis): boolean
⋮----
/**
   * Its first baseline from its top, which auto layouts aligning by baseline line up (a text's
   * first line), or `null` (its bottom is used).
   */
baseline(_el: E): number | null
⋮----
/** Hidden layers aren't snapped to. */
override snapTarget(el: E): boolean
⋮----
override fillDefaults(el: E): E
⋮----
// Files from before stroke alignment drew centered strokes.
⋮----
/** The images its paints show, so copies, exports and previews carry them. */
override assets(el: E): string[]
⋮----
override describe(el: E): ElementDescription
⋮----
/**
   * A new node from an agent's spec (`create_nodes`): the kind's own fields (`nodeFromSpec`),
   * then what every node takes (name, visibility, opacity, paints). The tool places it in a
   * container afterwards. Throws with a message the agent can act on.
   */
buildNode(spec: ElementSpec, index: string, context: NodeBuildContext): E
⋮----
/** The node a spec makes, at the top of the page; creatable kinds override it. */
protected nodeFromSpec(_spec: ElementSpec, _index: string, _context: NodeBuildContext): E
⋮----
/** Checks an agent's patch of the shared fields; subclasses check their own, then call this. */
override completePatch(
    el: E,
    patch: ElementPatch<E>,
    context: ElementBuildContext,
): ElementPatch<E>
</file>
