<file path="docs/plugins.md">
# Plugins

A plugin adds to Cloudy Canvas without changing its source: element types, tools, toolbar buttons, options panels, side panels, overlays, library items and **agent (MCP) tools**. It's a [module](../CLAUDE.md#modules), the same as the built-in features, loaded from disk when the app starts.

> Plugins run with the same access as the app: your files, the network and your boards. The app asks before a plugin runs for the first time. Only turn on plugins you trust.

## Format (API version 1)

A plugin is a folder:

```
my-plugin/
  plugin.json
  main.js
  …any other files (icons, data), read with api.plugin.readAsset / readText
```

`plugin.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "my-plugin",
  "name": "My plugin",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "What it adds.",
  "author": "You",
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "products": ["board"],
  "main": "main.js"
}
```

- `id`: lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Module ids must be the plugin id or start with `<id>.`.
- `main`: **one ES module with no imports.** Everything comes from `api`. If you write it in TypeScript or JSX, bundle it into one file and use `api.ui.React.createElement` as the JSX factory. Never bundle your own React.

- `products`: `["board"]`, `["design"]` or both.

`main.js` exports `activate(api)` by default, returning one module or a list of them (for the one product in `products`), or `{ board: [...], design: [...] }` for a plugin of both:

```js
export default function activate(api) {
  return api.core.defineModule({
    id: "my-plugin",
    register(host) {
      host.contribute(api.board.canvas.kinds, new MyKind());
      host.contribute(api.board.editor.tools, {
        tool: "my-tool",
        element: "my-type", // named and described by the element's kind
        icon: { svg: "<svg…>" },
        toolbar: { group: 1, order: 200 }, // leave it out to keep the tool off the toolbar
      });
    },
  });
}
```

## Tools: icon, name, description and placement

Each tool is one entry on `api.board.editor.tools`:

| Field                  | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tool`                 | The tool's id (the one given to `api.board.canvas.tools`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `icon`                 | A Lucide icon or `{ svg: "<svg…>" }` (drawn at the text's color with `currentColor`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `element`              | For a tool that adds an element: its type. The name and description come from the element kind's `label` and `description`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `label`, `description` | For other tools, instead of `element`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `toolbar`              | `{ group, order, menu }`: its button on the main toolbar; tools with the same `menu` (e.g. `"shapes"` in designs) share one button with a chevron listing them. Group 0 holds select and hand, group 1 the tools that add elements (built-ins use orders 10 to 100, so 110 and up come after them). Leave it out to keep the tool off the toolbar. |
| `library`              | Its card in the library (Shift+I). Tools with an `element` are listed by default; `{ section, order, keywords }` changes where and how, and `false` keeps one out. Other tools are only listed with a placement.                                                                                                                                   |
| `subTools`             | `[{ id, label }]`: tools picked from this tool's panel, which keep its button active.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

So a plugin that adds an element always shows it in the library, with the icon, name and description it gave. Whether it also gets a toolbar button is its choice.

## The API

| `api.…`  | What it holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `plugin` | `id`, `manifest`, `readAsset(path)`, `readText(path)` (files in the plugin's folder)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `core`   | `defineModule`, `definePoint` (points other plugins can extend), `createId`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `canvas` | the kind bases `ElementKind` (set `rotatable` for elements that turn; the engine draws and hits them turned and your kind works unturned; override `scale(el, t)` so the Scale tool grows what you draw, e.g. a font size, with `scaleRect`/`scaleLength`, and set `scalable` when it can be scaled alone; list the fields of its look in `styleFields` so Copy and Paste properties carry them, and override `applyStyle(el, style)` when its size follows them), `BoxKind`, `TextBoxKind`, `LineKind`; `elementBounds`, `rotatePoint`, `toUnrotated`; gradients `gradientCss`, `gradientHandles`, `transformFromHandles`; `ELEMENT_DEFAULTS`, `createElementBase`, `defineService`, `selectAndEdit`; helpers `clamp`, `roundPoint`, `fitInView`, `pastThreshold` with `DRAW_THRESHOLD_PX`/`MOVE_THRESHOLD_PX`, `FreehandTool` (a freehand drawing tool's base), `smoothPoints`, and for text `textFont`, `measureTextBlock`, `fontFamilyList` (a kind's `fonts(el)` asks the engine to load the faces its text uses); for agent tools `asUndoStep`, `buildElement`, `summarizeElement` and the argument readers (`stringArg`, `optionalNumber`, …) |
| `ui`     | `React` (the app's own), `toast`, `notifyError`, `FloatingPanel`, `PanelDivider`, `ToolButton`, `OptionButton`, `ColorSwatch`, `ColorPalette`, `ExtensionIconView`, `useEngine`, `useEngineState`, `useService`, `useEngineElement`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `design` | see [Design plugins](#design-plugins)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `board`  | the points: `canvas` (kinds, tools, hostCommands, keybindings, options, links, resolveElements, withMembers, alignTarget, frames, onRemove, prepareCopies, pasteText, pasteImage), `editor` (tools, toolPanels, selectionPanels, sidePanels, topBar, overlays, sessionHooks, contextMenu), `agentTools`, `library`; plus `toolItem`, `requireBoard` and `palette`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

What each point takes is described in CLAUDE.md (Modules, Canvas engine, Elements) and in the types in `src/canvas/modules/canvas-points.types.ts` and `src/canvas-ui/modules/editor-points.types.ts`.

Agent tools are groups contributed to `api.board.agentTools`: `{ id, tools: ({ kinds }) => [{ name, description, inputSchema, run(host, args) }] }`. They're listed by the app's MCP server like the built-in ones, and `list_plugins` tells agents which plugin adds what. Tool names must be unique; a tool whose name is taken is left out.

## Design plugins

Designs are built from modules the same way, on their own points (`api.design`):

| `api.design.…` | What it holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `canvas`       | the design's canvas points (same as the board's, plus `view`, `drawOrder`, `clips`, `selectTarget`, `editElement`, `onMoved`; `scopes` and `guides` are the pages module's, `rulerFrame` and `frames` the core module's, and a page's ruler guides are read with `engine.guides()`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `editor`       | the editor points shared with the board (`tools`, `toolPanels`, `overlays`, `sessionHooks`, `contextMenu`, …) plus `leftTabs` (a tab of the left panel, with its rail button), `propertySections` (a section of the properties panel, shown `when` the selection fits), `toolSidebars` (what the properties panel shows while a tool is on, like the frame presets), `layerIcons` (layer icons for types no tool creates); the shared editor points include `toolbars` (a toolbar shown instead of the main one while its tools are on, like the vector edit mode) and `mainMenu` (groups in the logo's menu: engine commands or `run({ engine, navigate })`)                                                                                                                                    |
| `nodes`        | the kind bases: `DesignNodeKind` (every design element: name, parent, visibility, opacity, fills, strokes; a container overrides `contentClip(el)` to clip its children), `BoxShapeKind` (a box-drawn shape: `createNode`, `clickSize`) and `PointsShapeKind` (a shape outlined by `points(el)`: drawing and hit testing come with it); the tools: `NodeDrawTool` (the drawing gesture, template method) and `BoxDrawTool` (draws any `BoxShapeKind`: `new BoxDrawTool(ctx, kind)`); helpers `createNodeBase`, `isDesignNode`, `solidPaint`, `imagePaint`, `gradientPaint` (a gradient started as Figma does), `isGradientPaint`, `drawPaints` (solid, gradient and image paints), `traceBox`, `NODE_DEFAULTS`, `containerAt`, `parentFor`, `pointsInBox`, `pointInPolygon`, `distanceToOutline` |
| `network`      | vector networks: `polylineNetwork`, `polygonNetwork`, `rectNetwork`, `ellipseNetwork`, `placeNetwork`, `scaleNetwork`, `networkBounds`, `hitSegment`, `vertexAt`, `insideRegion`, `traceStrokes`, `traceRegions`, the edits (`splitSegment`, `connect`, `addVertex`, `moveVertices`, `setTangent`, `removeParts`, `cutSegment`, `bendSegment`, `toggleSmooth`), and the edit mode's `VectorEditTool`, `VECTOR_EDIT`, `VECTOR_TOOLS`. A shape converts to a vector on double-click when its `BoxShapeKind` gives a `vectorNetwork(el)`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `tree`         | `DESIGN_TREE`, the layer tree service (`api.ui.useService(api.design.tree).layers(engine.scope)`: the page on screen; `null` for every page)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `pages`        | `DESIGN_PAGES`, the pages service (`pages()`, `add`, `rename`, `duplicate`, `remove`, `reorder`, `moveNodes`); the page on screen is `engine.scope`, shown with `engine.setScope(id)`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `panel`        | `PanelSection`, `PanelIconButton`, `PanelAddButton`, `PropertyGrid`, `FieldBox`, `NumberField`, `HexInput`, `PercentInput`, `PaintField`, and fields bound to the selection: `NodeNumberField`, `NodeSelectField`, `NodeCheckbox` (`read(node)` and `patch(value)`, "Mixed" when nodes differ, one undo step), `sharedValue`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `sections`     | filters for `propertySections`' `when`: `ofType(...types)`, `allKinds((kind) => …)`, `someNodes`, `noNodes`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `hooks`        | `useSelectedNodes`, `useEditNodes` (patches as one undo step), `useMoveNodes`, `useDesignEngine`, `useDesignState`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Every design element extends `DesignNodeKind`, so the built-in sections (Position, Layout, Appearance, Fills, Strokes, Export) and the Layers tab work with it without extra code. Nodes carry the page they're on (`pageId`); `createNodeBase` leaves it empty and the canvas puts a node on the page on screen when it's added, so kinds and tools never set it. A shape outlined by corners only gives its points; `BoxDrawTool` draws it from the kind, so there's no tool to write. A star, for example:

```js
export default function activate(api) {
  const { PointsShapeKind, BoxDrawTool, createNodeBase, solidPaint, pointsInBox } =
    api.design.nodes;

  class StarKind extends PointsShapeKind {
    type = "my-star.star";
    label = "Star"; // also the base of its layers' names: "Star 1", "Star 2", …
    description = "A five-pointed star.";
    tool = "my-star.star";
    defaults = { size: { w: 100, h: 100 } }; // what a click places

    createNode(rect, name, index, parentId) {
      return createNodeBase(this.type, rect, index, {
        name,
        parentId,
        fills: [solidPaint("#FFC83D")],
      });
    }

    points(el) {
      return pointsInBox(10, (i) => (i % 2 ? 0.4 : 1), el.w, el.h);
    }
  }

  return api.core.defineModule({
    id: "my-star",
    register(host) {
      const kind = new StarKind();
      host.contribute(api.design.canvas.kinds, kind);
      host.contribute(api.design.canvas.tools, {
        id: kind.tool,
        create: (ctx) => new BoxDrawTool(ctx, kind),
        keys: [{ key: "s", shift: true }],
      });
      host.contribute(api.design.editor.tools, {
        tool: kind.tool,
        element: kind.type,
        icon: { svg: "<svg …>" },
        toolbar: { group: 1, order: 110, menu: "shapes" }, // in the shapes menu
      });
    },
  });
}
```

Tools that don't draw a box (like the line tool, which draws between two ends) extend `NodeDrawTool` and describe their shape: `dragShape`, `clickShape`, `createNode`, `shapePatch`.

Design agent tools are groups contributed to `api.design.agentTools`, like the board's (`run(host, args)` gets the design host; `api.design.requireDesign(host)` is the open design, `{ engine, path, … }`). A kind agents may create with `create_nodes` sets `creatable = true`, lists its own fields in `specProperties` and overrides `nodeFromSpec(spec, index, context)` (`BoxShapeKind` already does: `w`/`h` or its click size, named with `context.nameFor(label)`); `update_nodes` checks patches with its `completePatch` (call `super.completePatch` for the shared fields: paints, opacity, parent).

## Rules

- **Name everything after the plugin:** element types, tool ids, option keys and agent tool names, so they don't collide with the app or other plugins. When a plugin collides (a type, tool or command that's already taken, an option given twice), it's turned off with the reason shown in Settings › Plugins, and the board opens without it.
- Elements of a plugin that's off or uninstalled stay in the file untouched; they're just not shown until it's back.
- Plugins load once, when the app starts. Changes apply after a reload.
- Reading something that isn't in the API (a typo, or a name from another version, e.g. `api.board.editor.toolbar`) throws right away, naming it, and the plugin is marked as failed with that message.
- An installed (copied) plugin doesn't change when its source folder does: install it again to update it, or add the folder for development while you work on it.

## Trying one

1. Settings › Plugins › **Add folder for development…** and pick the plugin's folder. It's loaded from there on every start, so edit, then reload.
2. Turn it on (the app asks you to trust it), then press **Reload**.
3. **Install from folder…** copies a plugin into the app data folder (`<appData>/plugins/<id>/`), replacing an older copy.

`examples/plugins/callout/` is a complete plugin in plain JavaScript: an element type (`TextBoxKind`), its tool with the `O` key, a toolbar button with an SVG icon, a color panel and the `create_callout` agent tool.
</file>

<file path="src/canvas/canvas-product.types.ts">
import type { CanvasViewOptions } from "./canvas-view.types";
import type { CopyContext, PastedImage } from "./clipboard";
import type { CanvasDocument, EditedChange } from "./document";
import type { CanvasElement, ElementKinds, ElementPatch } from "./elements";
import type { Point, Rect } from "./geometry.types";
import type { Keybindings } from "./input";
import type { EffectRenderers, ElementClip, ElementEffects, ElementMasks } from "./render";
import type { CanvasGuides } from "./ruler-guides";
import type { CanvasLinks } from "./links";
import type { Tool, ToolContext } from "./tools";
⋮----
/**
 * What makes a canvas a board or a design file: its element types, its tools, its shortcuts and
 * its tool options. The engine is the same for every product; it's created with one of these.
 * `O` is the product's tool options (colors, sizes, … the options panel edits).
 */
export interface CanvasProduct<O extends object = object> {
  /** e.g. `"board"`; used in messages and logs. */
  readonly id: string;
  readonly kinds: ElementKinds<O>;
  /** The product's tools, added after the built-in select and hand tools. */
  createTools(ctx: ToolContext<O>): Tool[];
  /** Every command's shortcuts: `BASE_KEYBINDINGS` plus `tool.<id>` for the product's tools. */
  readonly keybindings: Keybindings;
  /**
   * Commands the host app implements (e.g. opening a panel), bound in `keybindings` like any other.
   * The host handles each with `engine.handleHostAction(id, handler)`.
   */
  readonly hostCommands?: readonly string[];
  /** Tool options a new editor starts with. */
  readonly defaultOptions: O;
  /** Zoom range and background grid; unset values are `DEFAULT_VIEW_OPTIONS`'. */
  readonly view?: Partial<CanvasViewOptions>;
  /**
   * Splits the document into scopes shown one at a time (a design's pages). Without it, the
   * canvas shows every element.
   */
  readonly scopes?: CanvasScopes;
  /** Where the ruler guides are kept (per scope). Without it, the canvas has none. */
  readonly guides?: CanvasGuides;
  /**
   * Drawing order keys (compared as strings, bottom to top) for elements whose order isn't their
   * own `index` alone, e.g. nodes of a tree drawn after their parent. Elements left out get
   * `zOrderKey`. `elements` are the scene's, with derived geometry resolved.
   */
  orderKeys?(elements: readonly CanvasElement[]): Map<string, string>;
  /**
   * The world area each clipped element shows in (e.g. children of a frame that clips its
   * content); elements left out aren't clipped. What's clipped away isn't drawn or hit.
   * `elements` are the scene's, with derived geometry resolved.
   */
  clips?(elements: readonly CanvasElement[]): Map<string, ElementClip>;
  /**
   * The masks: elements that others show through (only where the mask shows, or where it doesn't
   * when inverted), and where each element under one is drawn (see `ElementMasks`). What's masked
   * away isn't drawn or hit. `elements` are the scene's, with derived geometry resolved.
   */
  masks?(elements: readonly CanvasElement[]): ElementMasks;
  /**
   * Each element's effects (shadows, blurs, shaders) and what they're drawn over: the element and
   * what it holds (see `ElementEffects`). Its slots nest with the masks'. `elements` are the
   * scene's, with derived geometry resolved.
   */
  effects?(elements: readonly CanvasElement[]): ElementEffects;
  /** How each type of effect is drawn, by type (effects without one aren't drawn). */
  effectRenderers?: EffectRenderers;
  /**
   * Elements that are on the canvas (hit, selected, snapped to their parents' results) but not
   * drawn on their own, e.g. a boolean's operands, which it draws combined. `elements` are the
   * scene's, with derived geometry resolved.
   */
  undrawn?(elements: readonly CanvasElement[]): ReadonlySet<string>;
  /**
   * Starts editing an element in a way of its own (e.g. a design vector's points), on
   * double-click or Enter. Returns `false` to fall back to editing its text, if it has any.
   */
  editElement?(el: CanvasElement, ctx: ToolContext<O>): boolean;
  /**
   * What a click on the element `hitId` selects (e.g. the group holding it, as in Figma), given
   * the current selection: `deep` (Ctrl/Cmd+click) asks for the element itself, `enter`
   * (double-click) for one level further into a group. Without it, clicks select what they hit.
   */
  selectTarget?(
    hitId: string,
    request: SelectTargetRequest,
    elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  ): string;
  /**
   * What a single element is aligned with (the align commands): the box that holds it (e.g. a
   * design's parent frame, a board's section), or `null` when nothing does.
   */
  alignTarget?(el: CanvasElement, elements: readonly CanvasElement[]): Rect | null;
  /**
   * The frame the rulers measure for this selection (e.g. the design frame it's in, as in Figma):
   * they count from its top-left corner and number only its span (the page's while it's turned),
   * and a guide dragged out of them while it's set belongs to it. `null`, or without it, the whole
   * canvas from the world's origin.
   */
  rulerFrame?(
    selected: readonly CanvasElement[],
    elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  ): CanvasElement | null;
  /**
   * The frames N and Shift+N step through (`nextFrame`, `previousFrame`), in order (e.g. a
   * design's top-level frames, a board's sections, in reading order). Without it, none.
   */
  frames?(elements: readonly CanvasElement[]): readonly CanvasElement[];
  /**
   * Runs when the select tool finishes dragging elements (with their members) to a new place,
   * inside the drag's undo step: e.g. puts them into the frame they were dropped on. `elements`
   * are the scene's, after the move.
   */
  onMoved?(
    doc: CanvasDocument,
    moved: ReadonlySet<string>,
    elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
  ): void;
  /**
   * Runs after every edit, inside its transaction and undo step (`CanvasDocument.setAfterEdit`):
   * writes what follows from the change (e.g. a design's auto layout), which runs it again with
   * what that changed. Elements a file opens with don't run it.
   */
  afterEdit?(doc: CanvasDocument, change: EditedChange): void;
  /**
   * Gives elements whose geometry follows others (e.g. a box around a group) their current
   * geometry. Returns the list with those replaced by new objects and the rest as they were;
   * the replaced ones are redrawn on every change.
   */
  resolveElements?(elements: CanvasElement[]): CanvasElement[];
  /**
   * The ids plus what goes with them when they're moved or deleted (e.g. an entity's attributes).
   * `elements` are the scene's, with derived geometry resolved.
   */
  withMembers?(
    ids: ReadonlySet<string>,
    elements: readonly CanvasElement[],
    purpose: "move" | "delete",
  ): Set<string>;
  /** Lines derived from the elements, drawn under them (one set per engine). */
  createLinks?(): CanvasLinks[];
  /**
   * Cleans up after elements are deleted (e.g. clears references to them). Runs inside the
   * deletion's transaction, so it's part of the same undo step. `before` are the scene's elements
   * as they were before the deletion (derived geometry resolved).
   */
  onRemove?(
    doc: CanvasDocument,
    removed: ReadonlySet<string>,
    before: readonly CanvasElement[],
  ): void;
  /**
   * Fixes copied elements (pasted, duplicated or Alt-dragged) before they're added: unique names,
   * references to elements that weren't copied, … The copies already have new ids, with references
   * between them remapped. Returns the list to add.
   */
  prepareCopies?(copies: CanvasElement[], context: CopyContext): CanvasElement[];
  /**
   * An element for text pasted from outside the app, centered on `at` at z-order `index`, or
   * `null` to ignore it. `options` are the current tool options.
   */
  pasteText?(text: string, at: Point, index: string, options: O): CanvasElement | null;
  /**
   * Text pasted from outside the app while elements are selected, applied to them instead of
   * becoming an element (e.g. a CSS gradient as their fill): each element's patch, or `null` to
   * paste it as usual. Asked before `pasteText`.
   */
  pasteOnto?(text: string, selected: readonly CanvasElement[]): Map<string, ElementPatch> | null;
  /**
   * An element showing an image pasted or dropped from outside the app (stored as `image.assetId`),
   * fit and centered in `view` (the visible world rect, centered on the drop point for a drop) at
   * z-order `index`, or `null` to ignore it.
   */
  pasteImage?(image: PastedImage, view: Rect, index: string, options: O): CanvasElement | null;
}

place(el: CanvasElement, scope: string): CanvasElement;

<file path="CLAUDE.md">
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Cloudy Canvas (by DarkRedgm) is a desktop-first Figma + FigJam app built with Tauri 2, React 19, Vite, TypeScript (strict, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`), Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui (Radix), Zustand and React Router. One app holds two **products** on one shared canvas engine: **Board** (`.cboard`, FigJam-style; the editor is at `/board/:id` and is being rebuilt on the element architecture, see Elements) and **Design** (`.cdesign`, Figma-style; the editor is at `/design/:id`, built on modules from the start: frames and rectangles in a layer tree so far, see Design). Roadmap: desktop with local files, then a web build of the same frontend, then real-time collaboration (Yjs + Hocuspocus, Laravel backend). It must build on both Windows 11 and Arch Linux.

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm tauri dev      # desktop app
pnpm dev            # frontend only in a browser (native dialogs unavailable)
pnpm lint           # ESLint (flat config, eslint.config.js)
pnpm typecheck      # tsc for app + vite config (noEmit)
pnpm format         # Prettier (with tailwind plugin); format:check to verify
pnpm tauri build    # production bundle
pnpm release:linux  # AppImage (src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/)
pnpm release:arch   # pacman package (packaging/arch/PKGBUILD, needs makepkg):
                    # packaging/arch/cloudy-canvas-<ver>-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst, with the
                    # desktop entry, icons and the .cboard/.cdesign mime types
pnpm release:win    # Windows installer cross-built from Linux (cargo-xwin, NSIS):
                    # src-tauri/target/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/release/bundle/nsis/
pnpm release        # both
pnpm release:win:native  # on Windows itself: NSIS and MSI installers
pnpm release:tag 0.2.0   # bump the version, commit, tag v0.2.0 and push: CI builds a draft release
```

There is no test framework. **Verification is `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` only** (plus `pnpm format:check`). Do not run `tauri dev`, cargo, builds or browser checks to verify changes unless asked.

`VITE_MOCK_RECENTS=true` in `.env.local` (see `.env.example`) fills the Home "Recent files" grid with mock data in dev builds. `/design-system` is a dev-only page that previews tokens and components.

## Project structure

`src/` is the frontend (shared by the desktop app and the future web build). `src-tauri/` stays next to it: it's the Rust crate for the desktop shell, built by cargo, and the Tauri CLI expects it at the root.

```
src/
  app/          shell: entry, router, providers, theme sync, MCP server wiring (app/mcp)
  platform/     Tauri implementations of the shared/core interfaces (storage, dialogs, agent channel)
  shared/       app-wide, product-agnostic
    core/       plain TS: ids, files, keyboard, Storage/AgentChannel interfaces, MCP protocol
    ui/         design system: tokens, shadcn components, layout, hooks, brand
    stores/     Zustand stores for app UI state (theme, recent files, agent server)
    agent-server/  the "Agents" menu shown in every top bar
  canvas/       the canvas engine every product shares (plain TS, no React, no product code)
  canvas-ui/    React pieces every editor shares: hosting an engine, chrome components
  products/
    board/      engine side: its points, palette, shared agent tools, file format
      modules/  one folder per feature (its element types, tools, agent tools + `ui/` +
                `<name>.module.ts`), see Modules
      ui/       the board editor (React); composes the product from the modules
    design/     engine side: its points, file format and modules (core: the node base and the
                layer tree; frame, rectangle, layers, assets, plugins-tab)
      ui/       the design editor (React): rail, left panel, properties panel, toolbar
  pages/        app pages that aren't a product: home, settings, design-system
```

### Layering (enforced by ESLint `no-restricted-imports`)

Path aliases: `@app/*`, `@pages/*`, `@platform`, `@shared/*` (`@shared/core`, `@shared/ui/…`, `@shared/stores/…`, `@shared/agent-server`), `@canvas`, `@canvas-ui`, `@board`, `@design` (`@board/ui`, `@design/ui` for the editors). They're defined in both `tsconfig.json` and `vite.config.ts`, so keep the two in sync (`components.json` uses them too).

- **Engine code is plain TypeScript**, so the web version can reuse it: `shared/core`, `canvas/`, and `products/*` outside their UI (`ui/`, `modules/*/ui/`, `modules/*/*.module.ts`) may not import a product's UI, React, UI layers (`@shared/ui`, `@shared/stores`, `@canvas-ui`, `@pages`, `@app`) or platform code (`@platform`, `@tauri-apps/*`).
- **Lower layers never know higher ones:** `shared/` can't import `@canvas`/`@canvas-ui`; `shared/`, `canvas/` and `canvas-ui/` can't import products. **Products can't import each other.**
- A product's `ui/` uses its own engine side through its barrel (`@board`), plus `@canvas`, `@canvas-ui` and `@shared/*`. Module files and module `ui/` reach the editor's pieces with deep imports (`@board/ui/board-engine-context`).
- Platform access goes through interfaces in `shared/core` (e.g. `Storage` in `storage.types.ts`), implemented in `platform/` (Tauri).
- Business logic lives in TypeScript, not Rust. `src-tauri/` registers plugins (dialog, fs, clipboard-manager, opener, single-instance, deep-link), holds window config/capabilities and file associations, runs the agent server's HTTP transport (`src-tauri/src/mcp/`, which carries no MCP logic), lists the installed fonts (`src-tauri/src/system_fonts.rs`, `fontdb`), hands over the paths the OS asks to open (`src-tauri/src/open_files.rs`) and the `cloudy-canvas://` links it opens (`src-tauri/src/app_links.rs`).
- Ids come from `createId()` (`crypto.randomUUID()`), never auto-increment.
- Zustand stores (`shared/stores/`) hold app UI state only, never canvas content.

## Canvas engine (`src/canvas/`)

The engine is the same for every product. **A product is a `CanvasProduct`** (`canvas-product.types.ts`): its `kinds` (`ElementKinds`), `createTools(ctx)` (added after the built-in select and hand tools), `keybindings` and `defaultOptions`. `O` is the product's tool options type, threaded through `CanvasEngine<O>`, `ElementKind<E, O>`, `ToolContext<O>` and `EngineState<O>`. Products are assembled from modules with `composeProduct` (see Modules): the board's is `getBoardProduct()` (`products/board/ui/modules/board-modules.ts`), the design's `getDesignProduct()` (`products/design/ui/modules/design-modules.ts`).

- **Services** (`canvas/services/`): `defineService(id, (doc) => facade)` is a typed token, and `engine.service(def)` (or `ctx.service(def)` in tools, `useService(def)` in React) creates the facade on first use, once per engine. Facades must need no cleanup (they observe through a `DocumentFeed`). The board's are `DB_SCHEMA` (`DbSchema`) and `ER_MODEL` (`ErModel`).

- `CanvasEngine` (`canvas-engine.ts`) is a coordinator, created with `{ product, theme, document? }`. It wires the pieces together:
  - `CanvasDocument`: the content, a Yjs doc.
  - `Camera`
  - `Scene`: element list, selection, hover and marquee, plus spatial queries.
  - `Renderer`: PixiJS.
  - The tools.
  - Input modules: pointer, wheel and keyboard.
  - `TextEditor`: a DOM textarea overlay. Tools type a new element's text with `ctx.editNewText(draft)`: the draft is added to the document (and selected) only when the edit is committed with some text. An element with several texts (a table's cells) names each with a `part` key (`ElementText.partAt`/`partBox`/`nextPart`/`firstPart`): double-click edits the part under the pointer, Tab moves to the next, and only that part's text slot is hidden while editing.
  - **Rich text** (`text/rich/`, `text/rich-editor/`): a text with styled ranges is `TextRun`s (`{ start, end, style }`, UTF-16 indexes, the style the product's; `normalizeRuns`, `spliceRuns`, `styleRuns`, `clearRunFields`, `runsForText` move and split them as the text changes) over styled `RichSpan`s, which `layoutRichText(text, spans, frame)` lays out (`RichTextLayout`: lines of fragments, words wrapping greedily across spans, a line as tall as its tallest span, every span on one baseline centered in its own line height, align and justify), measured with `measureSpan`/`spanOffsets` and `fontMetrics` (Pixi's, dropped by `fontsChanged` when a font loads; caches key on `fontsVersion()`, and the engine re-syncs the views using it). `ElementView.placeRichText(layout, alpha)` draws it into one canvas texture (`RichTextSprite`, `drawRichText`: fragments on their baselines, `decorationRect` underlines and strikethroughs; drawn white for `setPaintTextMask`). A kind with `ElementText.rich` (`RichTextSpec`: `runs`, `layout`, `apply`, `shortcut`) is edited by a `RichTextSession` instead of the textarea: a hidden textarea takes typing, IME and the clipboard (its value is the text), the canvas redraws the element as edited (`renderer.previewElement`, or the draft layer for a new one), the caret and highlight are DOM (`RichEditorOverlay`) from the same layout (`rich-caret.ts`: `caretRect`, `selectionRects`, `indexAt`, `wordRange`), clicks/drags/double and triple clicks select (`pointerSelect`), Up/Down/Home/End move by layout lines, Ctrl+B/I/U and Ctrl+Shift+X toggle styles, and the session keeps its own undo (`SessionHistory`), written as one document step when it ends. Focus moving to the app's controls keeps it open; `EngineState.textSelection`, `engine.editingText()` and `engine.styleTextRange(patch)` (on what's typed next with only a caret) are what panels use.
  - **Line heights below the font's own** center each line's glyphs in it as CSS and Figma do (they reach past the line): `ElementView.placeText` moves Pixi's text up by `negativeHalfLeading` (`render/text-leading.ts`; Pixi starts every line at its top) and aligns by the lines' height, and the design's glyph outlines (`textOutline`) place baselines the same way.
  - **Text and fonts** (`text/`): text is shaped by a `TextFont` (`textFont(size, options)`: family, weight, style, line height, letter spacing; the app's Inter by default), which drawing (`canvasTextStyle`, `view.placeText`, alignment left/center/right/justify, top/middle/bottom), measuring (`measureTextBlock`; `measureText`/`measureWrapped` are its app-font shorthands) and the editor (`textEditorStyle`) share. An element's text sizing is `fitContent`, `fitHeight` or, per element, `text.sizing(el)` (`content`/`height`/`fixed`). Kinds name the faces their text uses with `fonts(el)` (`FontRequest`); the engine's `FontTracker` loads each once through `CanvasEngineOptions.fonts` (a `FontLoader`; `useCanvasEngine` passes `fontLibrary` from `@platform`), then redraws the elements using it (`ElementView.refreshText`) after their kind's `fontsLoaded(el)` patch (e.g. an auto-sized text's new size, outside the undo history). Fonts are `FontLibrary` (`shared/core/fonts/`: types, weights and names, `closestVariant`, Google catalog and CSS parsing): `platform/fonts/` lists installed families (the Rust `system_fonts` command) and Google's (`fonts.google.com/metadata/fonts`, cached a week, a short fallback list offline), and loads a Google face as `FontFace`s from its CSS, caching the files in `<appData>/fonts/`.

  It exposes `kinds`, `keymap`, `commands` and `elementInfo(type)` to hosts. `mount(container, onLoading?)` opens the canvas fitted to its content (at most 100%): it builds the views a slice at a time (`Renderer.syncElementsChunked`, about 12 ms per frame), then waits for the scope's images (`Renderer.preloadImages`) and fonts (`FontTracker.settled`), at most 8 s, reporting each step as an `EngineLoading`; input starts once it resolves. `useCanvasEngine` returns `{ engine, loading }` and both editors show `CanvasLoadingOverlay` (`canvas-ui`) until the engine is there. Hosts close it with `engine.close()` (`useCanvasEngine` does on unmount): input stops, the tasks set with `engine.onClose(key, task)` run while it can still draw (at most 3 s), then it's destroyed. `engine.thumbnail({ width, height })` is a small JPEG of the whole canvas framed to that size (`export/thumbnail.ts`), or `null` when it's empty.

- **Registries are per product, never global.** Everything that needs an element's kind (document, scene, renderer, overlay, text editor, tools via `ctx.kinds`, agent helpers) gets the product's `ElementKinds` and calls `kinds.kindOf(el)`.
- **Content lives only in the Yjs doc.** Each element is a `Y.Map` inside the `"shapes"` map (the name is kept so existing files load). Order is a fractional-index string (`index`), and lexicographic order is z-order.
  - All edits go through `CanvasDocument` methods (`add`, `update`, `updateMany`, `remove`), which transact with `LOCAL_ORIGIN` so `Y.UndoManager` tracks only local changes.
  - Call `doc.checkpoint()` before a user action to start a new undo step.
  - Binary data (image files) lives in the doc's `"assets"` map (`doc.addAsset`, `doc.getAsset`), keyed by a `createId()` id that elements point at. It's outside the undo history and shared by copies of an element; nothing deletes unused assets yet. Kinds name the assets an element shows with `kind.assets(el)`. The renderer decodes each one once into a texture (`render/image-cache.ts`; SVGs are rasterized first, `render/svg-image.ts`), and a drawer shows it with `view.placeImage(assetId, box, fit?)` (proportions kept: `contain`, the default, or `cover`, which crops). SVG icons are drawn with `view.placeIcon(key, svg, box)`, parsed once per icon.
  - The document's own **title and description** live in its `"meta"` map (`doc.meta()`, `doc.setMeta(patch)`, `doc.observeMeta`; undoable like elements). The title is shown instead of the file name when set (`displayName(file)` in `shared/core`); `useDocumentMeta(doc)` (`canvas-ui`) reads it in React. `doc.onChange(listener)` fires on any change (elements, view state, assets, meta): it's what dirty tracking and autosave listen to.
  - A document reads elements through the product's kinds (`new CanvasDocument(kinds)`, `CanvasDocument.fromUpdate(kinds, bytes)`): `doc.get`/`doc.all` return only registered types, with `kind.fillDefaults` applied. Elements of unregistered types (e.g. DB or ER shapes in older boards) stay in the doc untouched but aren't shown.
- **Data flow is one-way.** Tools write to the document, and `doc.observe` reports `{ updated, removed }` ids. The engine then refreshes the `Scene`, syncs only the changed Pixi views (`render/layers/element-layer.ts`) and requests a frame.
  - Rendering is on demand: Pixi uses `autoStart: false`, and `FrameScheduler` renders at most once per animation frame.
  - **Render cost:** each frame, views outside `camera.visibleWorldRect()` are culled (`ElementView.cull`, from its cached drawn `extent()`). A clipped view gets a mask only when the clip cuts something off (`clipCovers`). Text textures are capped by their element's size (`cappedTextResolution`, at most 4096 px a side; resolution at most 4), and image textures are scaled down to 4096 px when decoded (`ImageCache`).
- **Tools** implement `Tool` (`tools/tool.types.ts`, `id: string`) and act only through `ToolContext`, never through the engine directly. Select and hand are built in (`createBaseTools`); a product adds its own in `createTools`. A tool previews an element it's creating with `ctx.setDraft(el)`: the draft layer draws it with its kind, like any element. Other gesture feedback (a line being dragged, a drop target) is a `Guide` set with `ctx.setGuide(fn)`, drawn above the elements. `ctx.setFaded(ids)` dims elements a gesture is about to remove (the eraser); switching tools clears it. `ctx.animateIn(ids)` plays a quick pop on elements a tool just added (`render/entrance.ts`; the element layers advance it each frame and the engine keeps requesting frames while it plays; skipped with reduced motion).
- **Product hooks** keep product features out of the engine:
  - `createLinks()` returns `CanvasLinks` (`links/`): lines derived from the elements (e.g. database relations), re-resolved on every document change and drawn under the elements, highlighted when they touch the selection.
  - Links can show text with `view.label(text, at, options)` (pooled text nodes, e.g. ER cardinalities).
  - **Element actions and DOM overlays:** a kind's `interactionAt` press can call `ctx.activate(elementId, action)` for something only the host can do (play a video, open a link); hosts listen with `engine.onElementAction`. DOM placed over an element follows it with `engine.worldRectToScreen(rect)` and `engine.onViewChange(listener)` (camera, resize and document changes).
  - `resolveElements(elements)` gives elements whose geometry follows others (ER aggregation boxes, constraints) their current geometry: `Scene.refresh()` runs it, and the elements it replaced are redrawn on every change. **Read geometry from the scene** (`engine.getElement`, `ctx.getElement`), not from `doc.get`; the stored bounds of derived elements are stale. The text editor places itself from the scene too.
  - `withMembers(ids, elements, purpose)` adds what goes with the ids when they're moved (`ctx.withMembers` in the select tool) or deleted (`engine.deleteElements`), e.g. an entity's attributes.
  - `onRemove(doc, removed, before)` cleans up after deletions (e.g. clears refs to deleted tables, frees connector ends), inside the same undo step. `before` is the scene as it was, so resolved geometry of removed elements is still readable.
  - `prepareCopies(copies, { copied, existing })` fixes copied elements before they're added (the board: free DB names via `prepareDbCopies`, a new ER diagram per source diagram via `prepareErCopies`, loose connector ends via `prepareConnectorCopies`). `pasteText(text, at, index, options)` turns text pasted from outside the app into an element (the board: a text element), and `pasteImage(image, view, index, options)` an image (the board: an image element, `createPastedImage`).
- **Scopes** (`CanvasScopes`, the product's `scopes`, one module at most): a document split into parts shown one at a time (the design's pages). `list(doc)` is the scope ids in order, `of(el)` an element's scope (`null`: never shown, e.g. the page records) and `place(el, scope)` puts a new element in one. The `Scene` holds only the current scope's elements (`Scene.scope`, `scopeIds`), so hits, selection, exports, thumbnails, links and agents' `engine.elements()` stay in it; `doc.setPlacement` (set by the engine) places every added element in the scope on screen, so tools, pastes and agents need no code for it. `engine.scope`/`engine.setScope(id)` (and `EngineState.scope`): switching clears the selection, goes back to the select tool and restores that scope's camera (or fits its content). When the scope on screen is deleted the next one shows; an undo or redo that only touched another scope shows that one. Elements updated into another scope leave the canvas like removed ones. `doc.addUntracked` adds outside the undo history (what a file needs when it opens).
- **View, order and drops:** `view` (`CanvasViewOptions`: `minZoom`, `maxZoom`, `grid`: `"dots"`, `"pixels"`, a one-unit grid drawn over the content from 800%, or `"none"`; unset values are `DEFAULT_VIEW_OPTIONS`, the board's) sets the camera's limits and the grid layer (`render/layers/create-grid-layer.ts`). `orderKeys(elements)` replaces `zOrderKey` as the drawing order (the design's layer tree): `Scene.orderKey` is what `ElementLayer` stacks by, and `Scene.restackedIds` are redrawn when a key changes without its element (a parent moved in the order). `clips(elements)` gives the world area clipped elements show in (`ElementClip`: a rect and a corner radius): `Scene.clipOf` is what `ElementLayer` masks views with (`ElementView.setClip`; layers get `LayerPlacement`: `orderOf` and `clipOf`), `Scene.elementAt` ignores clicks on clipped-away parts, and `Scene.replacedIds` (order or clip changed) are placed again. `editElement(el, ctx)` (point `editElement`) edits an element its own way on double-click (after groups are entered) and Enter, before its text (the design's vector edit mode). Tools may have `onActivate()` (feedback that stays while they're on) and `onCommand(command)`, which every command asks first (`engine.toolTakes`), so a mode can own Esc, Enter, Delete and Ctrl+A; `ctx.getTool()` is the active one. The editor point `toolbars` (`ToolbarModeEntry`: `tools`, `component`) replaces the main toolbar while one of its tools is on (`ModuleToolbar`). `selectTarget(hitId, { selection, deep, enter }, elements)` decides what a click selects (`ctx.targetAt`, `ctx.targetOf`; the select tool, double-click and right-click use it; e.g. a design group). `FreehandTool` (`tools/freehand-tool.ts`) is the base of freehand drawing tools (the board's marker, the design's pencil): it collects, previews, smooths (`smoothPoints`, `smooth-points.ts`) and adds. `onMoved(doc, moved, elements)` runs when the select tool finishes a drag (`ctx.moved`), in the drag's undo step (the design drops nodes into frames). The canvas theme is read from the editor's container (`readCanvasTheme(container)`), so a product can override the `--canvas-*` tokens (`[data-product="design"]` in `tokens.css`).
- **Paths** (`canvas/path/`, plain TS): a `PathShape` is contours of cubic `PathSegment`s (`PathContour { start, segments, closed, hole? }`; a closed contour's last segment ends at its start). `booleanPaths(op, operands)` (`union`, `subtract`: the first minus the rest, `intersect`, `exclude`; each `PathOperand` filled by its own `fillRule`) and `normalizePath(shape, fillRule)` (overlaps and self-crossings resolved into outers followed by their holes) run Clipper2 (`clipper2-ts`) on flattened integer paths (`flattenContour`, adaptive to `FLATTEN_TOLERANCE`, ×`PATH_SCALE`) whose points carry `SourceTags` in `z` (the curve and `t` each came from; Clipper's Z callback tags crossings), so `rebuildContour` turns the result back into the source curves' exact parts (`subCurve`). `outlineStroke(shape, { width, cap, join, miterLimit })` is a stroke's area (`ClipperOffset`); `strokeArea(shape, { …, align, dashes, dashOffset })` lays it `inside`/`center`/`outside` (twice as wide, cut by what the closed contours enclose; open ones stay centered) after `dashPath(shape, pattern, offset)` (dashes as open parts of the source curves by arc length, an odd pattern repeated, the dash over a closed contour's start joined); `rectPath(rect, radius)` is a (rounded) box and `boxSidesStroke(w, h, radius, sides, align)` a box's band with a weight per side (`BoxSides`). Also `pathBounds` (exact curve extremes), `pointInPath` (even-odd over normalized contours) and `distanceToPath`, `placePath`/`localPath`/`mapPath`, the bezier helpers (`pointAt`, `splitAt`, `subCurve`, `flatness`, …) and `fillPath(g, shape, style)` (each outer filled, its holes `cut()`) / `strokePath`. `LruCache` and `identityKey` (`canvas/utils`) cache what's worked out from shapes.
- **Images in a box** (`canvas/image/`, plain TS): an `ImageTransform` is Figma's `imageTransform` (2×3, the layer's normalized box → the picture's), an `ImageCrop` the axis-aligned case (`cropTransform`/`transformCrop`), `ImageRotation` quarter turns and `ImagePlacement` what the renderer takes (`contain`/`cover` with a rotation, `transform`, `tile` with a scale). Helpers: `fitTransform` (the transform that looks like contain/cover), `imageQuad`, `panTransform`, `zoomTransform`, `reframeTransform` (the box changes, the picture stays), `rotateTransform90`, `clampCrop`, `cropInside`, `coverCrop`. `ImagePaintLayer.placement` is drawn by `PaintStack`'s image slot (a sprite placed with `imageMatrix`, or a `TilingSprite` whose tiles use the picture's own size, `ImageCache.naturalSize`); `view.placeImage(assetId, box, fit | crop)` crops the texture's frame (`fitImage`). `ImageCropOverlay` (`canvas-ui/components/image-crop/`, pure drag math in `crop-drag.ts`) edits one: the picture dimmed past the box, drag to move, its corners scale it (Alt: round its middle), the box's sides resize the element (Shift keeps the ratio), Enter/Esc finish; `clamp` keeps the crop inside the picture. Overlays map boxes to the screen with `canvas-ui/overlay/` (`normalizedToScreen`, `screenToNormalized`, `screenToLocal`, `useViewMapping`), and `useAssetUrl` shows an asset in the DOM.
- **Effects** (`canvas/effects/` data, `render/effects/` drawing): a `CanvasEffect` (`id`, `type`, `visible`, plus its type's fields) is plain JSON; the product's `effectRenderers` (point `effectRenderers`, keyed by type) draw them on the GPU and its `effects(elements)` hook (one module) returns `ElementEffects`: an `EffectScope` per element with effects (`effects`, `home`, `box`, `rotation`, `bounds` of what it holds) and `homes` (element → its `EffectSlot`). Slots are a `ScopeSlot` (`MaskSlot | EffectSlot`), so masks' and effects' scopes nest in each other (`homeOf`, `scopeHome`, `sameSlot` in `layer-placement.ts`; a product gives both consistently, the design through `treeSlots`); `Scene.effects`, `Scene.visualBounds(el)` (shown bounds grown by `effectsOutset`, what exports frame) and `masksOf` walk them. `ElementLayer` puts an element's view and what it holds into an `EffectScopeView` (`render/layers/effect-scope-view.ts`: at the element's order key, clipped like its view, culled with its reach) whose one `EffectStackFilter` (a Pixi `Filter` overriding `apply`) runs the effects' `EffectRenderer`s stage by stage (`backdrop`, `content`, `behind`, `filter`) over the content texture, each `render(pass, effect, current)` returning the new result. An `EffectPass` gives `content`, `backdrop` (the back texture, for renderers with `backdrop`/`readsBackdrop`; the canvas then keeps Pixi's back buffer, `RendererOptions.backdrop`), `px`/`offset` (world → CSS px, turned with the element), `toLocal` (texture coordinates → the element's own), `texture()`, `run(shader, input)` and a Gaussian `blur(input, radius)` (`blurShader`, taps spread past `MAX_BLUR_TAPS`); textures are pooled and returned after. `EffectShader` wraps a GLSL ES 3 fragment (highp; `FILTER_HEADER`, `SAMPLING_GLSL`: `sampleIn`, `px`) with its uniforms (`set`) and samplers (`bind`); shared ones: `copyShader`, `silhouetteShader` (offset, round spread, invert, color), `underShader`, `atopShader`, `shapeUnderShader`. `ElementLayer.setEffectScale` is the zoom (1 in snapshots); on the canvas renderer effects are skipped. **Compositing:** an `EffectScope` may carry a `composite` (`ScopeComposite`: `opacity`, a `BlendMode` from `canvas/effects/` (`BLEND_MODES`, Figma's eighteen), `isolated`): the filter's last step is `compositeShader` (`render/effects/composite-shader.ts`, the W3C formulas over `pass.backdrop`, so the canvas keeps the back buffer for products with an `effects` hook), and a non-isolated opacity-only scope with no effects runs no filter, its container's `alpha` handing the opacity down. Paint layers take a `blendMode` too (`pixiBlendMode`: Pixi's own modes, `pixi.js/advanced-blend-modes` registered by the renderer; hue draws normal).
- **Undrawn elements:** the product's `undrawn(elements)` hook (one module) names elements that are hit, selected and moved but not drawn on their own (a design boolean's operands, which it draws combined): `Scene.drawn(el)`, `LayerPlacement.drawn`, `ElementView.setDrawn` (a view with an empty clip, what a hidden parent holds, isn't drawn either); snapping skips them. `engine.refreshElements(ids)` reads elements again with what derives from them though the document didn't change (a text's glyph outlines arrived).
- **Masks** (Figma's, `render/layer-placement.types.ts`): the product's `masks(elements)` hook (one module) returns `ElementMasks`: each `ElementMask` (`id`, `mode`: `alpha`/`vector`/`luminance`, `inverted`, `home`: the `MaskSlot` its scope sits in, `bounds`, `shape`: world-placed `MaskShape`s (`path`, drawn with holes) for a vector mask or `null`, `contains(p)`) and `homes` (element → its innermost `MaskSlot`: `{ mask, role: "source" | "masked" }`). The scene keeps them (`Scene.masks`, `masksOf(el)`, a changed slot is in `replacedIds`); `elementAt` skips what a mask hides, `shownBounds(el)` (bounds ∩ clip ∩ the masks it shows through) is what marquees, snapping, exports and thumbnails read, and the overlay outlines the hovered (or single selected) element's masks dashed (`OverlayState.masks`). `ElementLayer` nests views: each mask is a `MaskScopeView` (in its home's container at the mask's order key) holding a `MaskSource` (the mask's views, never drawn on their own: rendered into the mask's texture, an `AlphaMask` through the `MaskSourceEffect` Pixi extension) and the masked views; `luminance` puts brightness in the red channel with a `ColorMatrixFilter`, `vector` is a stencil of the outlines (or the source made opaque when a part has none), `inverted` is Pixi's inverse mask. A scope off screen is culled and its texture covers only what's on screen (`boundsArea`).
- **Frames:** a kind with `frame = true` (ER aggregation boxes, sections) is drawn in its own layer behind the links and the other elements, larger frames further back (`zOrderKey`, `elements/z-order.ts`), and a marquee selects it only when it encloses it.
- **Feeds:** board-level facades (`DbSchema`, `ErModel`) notify React through a `DocumentFeed` (`document/document-feed.ts`), which observes the document only while someone subscribes, so they need no cleanup and can be created in a `useMemo`.
  - Kinds offer `interactionAt` and `handles` (see Elements), which the select tool and overlay use.
- **Copy and paste** (`clipboard/`): `ElementClipboard` copies the selection with what moves with it (`withMembers(…, "move")`), as scene elements, to the system clipboard as JSON (`encodeClipboard`/`decodeClipboard`, tagged with the product id, with the assets they show in base64 so images paste into other files). `insertCopies` clones them (`cloneElements`: fresh ids and indexes, and `remapIds` rewrites every string equal to a copied id, so references between copies follow without knowing the types), runs the product's `prepareCopies`, offsets them with `kind.move` and adds them as one undo step. Pastes land 20 units further each time while the source is in view, otherwise centered in it. Anything else on the clipboard goes through `paste-external.ts`: an image (preferred over text) becomes an asset plus the product's `pasteImage` element, and text goes to `pasteText`. Files dropped on an open editor go the same way (`drop-files.ts`, `engine.dropFiles(files, clientPoint)`): images and SVGs through `pasteImage` (fit and centered on the drop point; SVGs are sized by `svgSize`), `.txt` files through `pasteText`, cascaded by a paste step, as one undo step. The system clipboard is the `Clipboard` interface (`shared/core/clipboard.types.ts`: text, plus `readImage()` as an encoded file; `platform/clipboard.ts`: Tauri's clipboard manager, whose RGBA images are encoded to PNG, or `navigator.clipboard` in the browser), passed as `CanvasEngineOptions.clipboard` by `useCanvasEngine`; without one, the engine uses a `MemoryClipboard`. The commands are `copy`, `cut`, `paste` and `duplicate` (Ctrl+D). Alt-dragging with the select tool duplicates in place (`ctx.duplicate`) and drags the copies.
- **Context menu, z-order, lock and export:** a right-click selects what's under the pointer (locked elements too; empty space clears the selection) and reports a `ContextMenuRequest` to `engine.onContextMenu` listeners; `CanvasContextMenu` (`canvas-ui/components/context-menu/`) shows it, its items are data (`SELECTION_MENU`, `CANVAS_MENU`: engine commands, labels from `BASE_COMMAND_LABELS`; a `ContextMenuCategory` is a submenu of commands, like Copy/Paste as and Order, and a module's `contextMenu` group with a `label` becomes one, like the design's Transform, Mask and Boolean, so the menu stays short; menus past the window's height scroll, `MENU_FITS_SCREEN`). `reorderSelection` (`bringToFront` `]`, `bringForward` Ctrl+], `sendBackward` Ctrl+[, `sendToBack` `[`) rewrites indexes with `reorderIndexes` (`elements/reorder.ts`: front/back of everything, or one step past the nearest overlapping element; frames keep their area order). An element with `locked` is skipped by `Scene.elementAt` (unless asked), `elementsInRect`, `findInteraction`, `selectAll` and the select tool's drags (`toggleLock` Ctrl+Shift+L, `unlockAll` Ctrl+Alt+Shift+L). `pasteToReplace` (Ctrl+Shift+R) pastes centered on the selection and removes it in the same undo step (`ElementClipboard.paste({ replace })`). Exports (`canvas/export/`): `engine.exportElements({ format, background, area })` draws the selection (with its `withMembers(…, "move")`) or the whole canvas off screen (`Renderer.snapshot`, fresh layers and the product's `createLinks()`, images loaded first) as PNG or JPG, a one-page PDF (`encodePdf`, a hand-written JPEG page) or CSV of the elements whose kind has `rows(el)` (tables, DB tables; `encodeCsv`). `copyAsPng` (Ctrl+Shift+C) writes one with `Clipboard.writeImage`. The `export` command (Ctrl+Shift+E) is a host action: `ExportDialog` (`canvas-ui/components/export-dialog/`) handles it and saves with `exportFile` from `@platform`.
- **Nudge, resize and size label:** the arrow keys nudge the selection (`nudgeLeft`…, Shift: `nudgeLeftFar`…, 10 units; `engine.nudgeSelection`, `engine.moveElements` with `withMembers(…, "move")`, locked ones stay, no `onMoved`, so nothing changes parent); a burst of presses is one undo step (`nudgeCheckpoint`, `canvas/arrange/nudge.ts`; tools take them with `onCommand` and `nudgeStep(command)`, e.g. vector edit mode nudges its points). The resize handles belong to a `ResizeTarget` (`handles/resize-target.ts`, `resizeTarget(selected, kinds)`): one resizable element, or a multi-selection with a resizable element in it, by the box round the outlined ones; `ResizeGesture` scales each element into the new box (`scaleRectInBox`, `geometry.ts`) through `kind.resize` (ones that can't resize move by their center, with their members). Shift (or any `keepsRatio` kind) keeps the proportions, Alt resizes round the center (`resizeRect(…, { keepRatio, fromCenter })`). `CanvasViewOptions.sizeLabel` (the design's) shows the selection's `W × H` in a tag under it (`render/layers/size-label-layer.ts`, from `OverlayState.size`).
- **Snapping and smart guides** (`canvas/snapping/`): a gesture asks `ctx.createSnapper(exclude)` (what it moves, with its members) for a `Snapper` (`GestureSnapper`) and calls `move(box, p)` (an offset for the moved box), `resize(box, handle, p)` (for the dragged sides) or `point(world, p)`, then `clear()` when it ends. Targets are collected on first use (`engine.snapTargets`: the scene's elements whose `kind.snapTarget(el)` is true (outlined ones; hidden design layers and groups aren't), clipped like they're drawn, on and around the screen) as sorted edge lists (`snapTargets`, `snap-edges.ts`: start, center and end lines, `nearestOffset`, `edgesAt`). A move snaps each axis to the nearest edge or to equal spacing (`equal-spacing.ts`: centered between its neighbors on the row, or repeating a gap of the row), whichever is closer within 5 screen px; with `pixelGrid`, axes nothing snapped are rounded to whole units. Ctrl/Cmd (`p.modKey`) turns object snapping off. The guides are a `SnapFeedback` (`lines` with × marks, `gaps` with their length) drawn in screen space by `render/layers/snap-layer.ts` in the `--canvas-snap` color (`CanvasTheme.snap`); `ctx.setSnapFeedback` shows any (the select tool's Alt + hover distances, `measureGaps`). Used by the select tool's moves, `ResizeGesture`, the design's `NodeDrawTool` and `LineEndDrag`. `SnapSettings` (`objects`, `pixelGrid`) start from `CanvasViewOptions.snapping` (the design's: both on; the board's: off), are `EngineState.snapping` and `engine.setSnapping(patch)`; `useCanvasEngine` applies the user's choice and `useSnapping()` (`canvas-ui`) changes and remembers it per product (`shared/stores/snapping-store.ts`). The toggles are in `ZoomMenu` ("Snap to pixel grid" only with the `pixels` grid).
- **Align, distribute and tidy up** (`canvas/arrange/`, pure functions over `ArrangeItem`s: `alignOffset`, `distributeOffsets` (the first and last stay, equal spaces, whole units), `tidyUpOffsets` (rows by middle, columns as wide as their widest item, the median spacing)): `arrangeItems` picks the outlined, unlocked ids that don't already move with another of them; the engine's `alignElements`/`distributeElements`/`tidyUpElements` (and the `…Selection` commands `alignLeft`, `alignCenterX`, `alignRight`, `alignTop`, `alignCenterY`, `alignBottom` (Alt+A/H/D/W/V/S, matched by `code`), `distributeHorizontal`/`distributeVertical` (Alt+Shift+H/V) and `tidyUp` (Alt+Shift+T)) move them with `moveElementsBy` (with their members) in one undo step, with no `onMoved`, so nothing changes parent. Several elements align with their bounds; one aligns with the product's `alignTarget` (the design: its nearest container, `containerAlignTarget`; the board: the smallest section it's in, `sectionAlignTarget`), and `engine.canAlign(ids)` says whether there's one. The selection's context menu has an "Align" submenu; the design's Position section has the buttons (`ArrangeButtons`).
- **Scale tool (K)** (Figma's): `ScaleTool` (`tools/scale-tool.ts`, a `SelectTool` with `resizeMode: "scale"`) is built in next to select and hand; products bind its key (`tool.scale`: K in the design, Shift+K on the board, where K is the sticker tool) and put it in the toolbar's `move` menu with select. The active tool's `Tool.resizeMode` is `Scene.resizeMode`, which `resizeTarget(selected, kinds, mode)`, `findInteraction` and the overlay read: in `scale` mode what's `scalable` gets handles (a line, a group, a board text too) and the box takes lines along. `ResizeGesture` in `scale` mode keeps the proportions and scales every element with its `withMembers(…, "move")` round the drag's fixed point (`resizeAnchor`: the opposite corner or side, the center with Alt; turned for a turned element) through `kind.scale(el, t)` (`ScaleTransform { origin, factor }`, `elements/element-scale.ts`: `scalePoint`, `scaleRect`, `scaleLength`, `scaleOffsets`; `scalePatches`, `canvas/arrange/scale.ts`). The default resizes a resizable element to its scaled box and moves the rest; `BoxKind` and `LineKind` (points) are `scalable`, and kinds scale what they draw: the design's nodes their `strokeWeight`, rectangles and frames their `cornerRadius`, texts `fontSize` and `letterSpacing` (laid out again), lines their ends, vectors their network (groups leave it to their children); the board's texts their `fontSize`, stickies and tables a `textScale` (font and insets, `tableTypography`), shapes their `fontSize` and `strokeWidth`, strokes and connectors their `size` (free connector ends move), images their `padding`; DB and ER elements only move. `engine.scaleElements(ids, factor, anchor)` (a `ScaleAnchor` of the box round them, `anchorPoint`, `SCALE_ANCHORS`) is one undo step: the design's `ScaleSidebar` (the tool's `toolSidebars` entry: W, H, %, the 3×3 `AnchorPicker`) and the agents' `scale_shapes`/`scale_nodes` (`canvas/agent/scale-tool.ts`, part of `arrangeTools`: `factor`, `width` or `height`, `anchor`) use it.
- **Zoom to selection and frames:** `zoomToSelection` (Shift+2) fits the selection (`engine.zoomToSelection()`, past 100% when it's small: `Camera.fitRect(rect, { padding, maxZoom })`, `FitOptions`; no selection: zoom to fit). `nextFrame`/`previousFrame` (N / Shift+N, `engine.zoomToFrame(1 | -1)`) fit and select the next or previous of the product's `frames(elements)` hook (one module; the design's top-level visible containers, `topFrames`; the board's sections, `boardSections`; both in `readingOrder`, `canvas/arrange/reading-order.ts`, rows as tidy up makes them): after the selected one or the one holding the selection (`withMembers(…, "move")`), else the one nearest the middle of the view, wrapping round. In the `ZoomMenu`, the selection's context menu and the design's View menu.
- **Copy and paste properties** (Figma's, Ctrl+Alt+C / Ctrl+Alt+V, matched by `code`): a kind lists the stored fields that make up its look in `styleFields`; `styleOf(el)` copies them (`ElementStyle`, plain JSON) and `applyStyle(el, style)` patches the ones it has too, matched **by name across types** (a rectangle's fills paste onto a text). `engine.copyStyle()` takes the first selected element's into a per-product slot that lives for the app session (`canvas/clipboard/style-clipboard.ts`, never the system clipboard; `hasCopiedStyle()`), `engine.pasteStyle(ids?)` applies it to the unlocked selection in one undo step and `engine.applyStyleOf(fromId, ids)` does the same from an element (agents' `copy_properties_to_nodes`/`copy_properties_to_shapes`, `canvas/agent/style-tool.ts`, part of `arrangeTools`). The design's nodes take `opacity`, `fills`, `strokes`, `strokeWeight` (`NODE_STYLE_FIELDS`; `nodeStylePatch` drops fills where `fillable` is off, strokes where `strokable` is, image paints from strokes and kinds without `imageFills`), rectangles and frames `cornerRadius`, texts their typography and alignment (set again with `retypeset`), lines their caps; groups nothing. The board's stickies, tables and sections their `color`, shapes `fill`, `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `fontSize`, texts `color` and `fontSize` (sized to their text again), strokes `color`, `size`, `pen`, connectors `color`, `size`, `style` and heads, images `background` and `padding` (`imagePaddingPatch`); DB and ER elements nothing. In the selection's context menu and the design's Edit menu.
- **Rotation** (Figma's model): `CanvasElement.rotation` is degrees counterclockwise round the element's top-left corner (`x`, `y`); `w`×`h` is its unturned size, so growing from the corner (text, vector re-wrapping, right/bottom resizes) needs no correction. Kinds opt in with `ElementKind.rotatable` (the design's nodes; board kinds don't) and turn with `kind.rotate(el, degrees, pivot)` (the corner orbits, `rotation` adds up; the design's line turns its ends instead and keeps 0). Kinds work unturned: `Scene.elementAt` and `findInteraction` hand them `toUnrotated(p, el)`, `ElementView` places, turns and culls the view (`rotation.ts`: `rotatePoint`, `rotatedBounds`, `rotatedBoundsAround`, `pointInRotatedRect`, `normalizeAngle`, `angleOf`). `elementBounds(kind, el)` is where an element shows (the box round it when turned): hits, marquees, snapping, arranging, exports, thumbnails and paste placement read it; resizing reads `kind.bounds`. `ElementClip.rotation` turns a clip (masks are drawn in the view's frame, `clipCovers` checks in the clip's; `clipBounds`). The overlay draws `Outline`s (rect + rotation); a single turned element's resize handles sit on its turned box (`ResizeTarget.rotation`, `resizeHandlePoint`/`resizeHandleAt`/`resizeCursor` take it) and `ResizeGesture.resizeTurned` resizes it in its own frame; in a multi-resize turned elements follow by their center.
